subject: [chip dv] Implement and use JTAG RV debugger model
body:
The debugger model is built on top of JTAG DMI agent. It
will eventually provide all debugging capabilities required
to adequately test the chip.

In this commit, it provides ability to execute abstract register
access command to read and write CPU registers (abstract memory
access and quick access commands are unsuported in the PULP
implementation), enter debug mode, issue halt request, resume
request and ndm reset request. The SBA access methods that
originally lived in a separate sba_access_utils_pkg are moved
into the model so that everything is in one place. 2 new SBA
access methods have been added for convenience.

The sba_access_reg_frontdoor uses the debugger handle to run
the SBA access method for chip level CSR reads and writes. This
unlocks the ability to read and write the full chip CSRs over SBA
by using our existing CSR utility methods.

Finally, the `chip_sw_rv_dm_ndm_reset_when_cpu_halted` test
sequence is updated to use the debugger to demonstrate the
abstract register access command and the SBA frontdoor method.

The chip_if now has additional probes into the CPU registers to
cross check what we read from the debugger matches the probed
value.

subject: [csrng/rtl] Fix state clearing of DRBG modules
body:
Each of the `csrng_ctr_drbg_*` modules has an enable input.  Setting
this input low clears the internal FIFOs and some FFs, but it does not
clear all FFs and it does not clear the FSMs.

A test sequence writing commands over the software interface and
randomly disabling and re-enabling CSRNG (constrained so that the
command sequence after each re-enable starts with Instantiate) was
triggering a *fatal alert*: `blk_enc_state_q` of `csrng_ctr_drbg_upd`
stayed `ReqSend` while CSRNG was disabled, and the `blk_enc` FSM
controls the pop input of the `updreq` FIFO, which got cleared by the
disable. Thus, in the first cycle after re-enabling CSRNG, that FSM
tried to pop from an empty FIFO, which triggered the fatal alert.

This commit clears the *entire* state of the DRBG modules when CSRNG is
disabled.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [csrng/rtl] Fix disable value of `entropy_src` FFs in `csrng_core`
body:
The `entropy_src_seed_q` and `entropy_src_fips_q` FFs are currently not
cleared on disable.  This means their value for the first command is
wrong, as the RTL relies on them being zero to correctly handle
*Instantiate* commands that do not use entropy from `entropy_src`: The
first *Instantiate* after re-enable does not have `cmd_entropy_avail`
yet, and if `flag0[1]` is set, the previous value of the seed and the
FIPS bit in those registers gets used instead of all-zeroes.  If the
previous value is also all-zeroes, there is no difference and this case
is handled correctly.  If the previous value is non-zero, this case is
handled incorrectly.

This commit fixes that problem by making the value after re-enable of
those registers equal to their value after reset.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [csrng_agent] Correct handling of invalid commands for coverage
body:
This commit fixes the sampling of illegal commands in `csrng_monitor`:
the DUT does not respond to these commands, so the monitor must not wait
for the ack in case of illegal commands.

This commit also refines the coverage crosses defined in
`csrng_agent_cov`; `csrng_cmd_cross` is split into two crosses:
- `csrng_cmd_clen_flag_cross` tracks the coverage of commands and their
  parameters (i.e., `clen` and `flag0`), and
- `csrng_cmd_clen_flag_sts_cross` tracks the coverage of commands,
  parameters, and the returned status.

The first cross tracks coverage of all command-parameter combinations,
and the second cross tracks coverage of the expected status responses
for all command-parameter combinations.  In the latter, illegal commands
are excluded because their status is not defined (as there is no
response to illegal commands).

subject: [ci] Add checks for empty test_suites (and more!)
body:
This commit adds scripts that check for empty test_suite targets and
targets that contain "banned" characters. It also re-homes the check for
test_suite targets that are not tagged "manual".

I'm adding these scripts after making a few mistakes while cleaning up a
BUILD file in PR #16401.

My first mistake was forgetting to unpack a tuple. I wound up inserting
the tuple's string representation, rather than one of the tuple's
elements, into a target name via `string.format()`. Surprisingly, this
is not an analysis-time failure! Bazel has no problem inserting
parentheses and commas into the target name.

If weird characters are in a target name, for some definition of
"weird", it was probably an accident. The new script returns an error
when it finds targets with weird characters.

The second mistake I made was defining a test_suite with a non-empty
`tests` parameter, where none of the labels actually existed. The result
is a test_suite that appears non-empty, but actually contains zero
tests.

I believe an empty test_suite indicates an error. The new script returns
an error if it finds any test_suite targets that contain zero tests.

Signed-off-by: Dan McArdle <dmcardle@google.com>

subject: [opentitantool] SPI port name aliases
body:
We currently have `ott bootstrap` and `ott spi ...` commands which use a
SPI port to communicate with a bootlader.  In the future, there will be
`ott spi tpm` subcommand to communicate with code running on OpenTitna
via SPI using the TPM protocol.  For these different uses, we want to
default to using different SPI ports.  (Dauntless uses the same SPI pins
for both, but OpenTitan uses the dedicated QSPI lines for bootstrapping,
but pinmux'ed lines for the TPM SPI communication.)

In order to support such various setups, this PR introduces SPI port
alias_of, the same way as exists for UART ports.  In particular, rather
than referring to spi instance "0", all the existing commands are
modified to default to a SPI instance called "BOOTSTRAP", the future
`ott spi tpm` command will default to a SPI instance called "TPM".

Various json configuration files will declare "BOOTSTRAP" and "TPM" to
be aliases of the particular transport instances, for HyperDebug with
CW310 for instance "BOOTSTRAP" will map to the new "QSPI" port, and
"TPM" will map to the existing "SPI2" port.

subject: [crypto] Consolidate the OTBN driver and make it stateless.
body:
Previously, the functional OTBN driver for cryptolib was split between
drivers/otbn.c and impl/otbn_util.c, with the latter providing a few
basic utility functions in terms of the former. The otbn_util.c version
also included a state struct which simply stated which app was loaded
into OTBN (if any).

This commit completely removes impl/otbn_util.c. It removes the state
struct and moves some functions to drivers/otbn.c while eliminating
others (for instance, `otbn_copy_data_to_otbn()` is replaced with
`otbn_dmem_write()`, since they have a very similar interface).
Accordingly, some of existing functions (including `otbn_dmem_write`)
are adjusted to be more intuitive to use (e.g. by using an `otbn_addr_t`
instead of a raw byte offset).

Overall, the purpose of this change is to make the driver easier to
understand, use, and test, with all the source code in one place. It
also fits better with the (stateless) cryptolib to remove the OTBN state
struct.

subject: [opentitantool] Atomically modify mode/value/pull
body:
The current gpio trait cannot avoid glitches, if a configuration file
declares that a certain pin needs to be e.g. open drain and high logical
level.  If the new level is applied before the open drain mode, and the
pin happened to be in push/pull mode before, strongly pulling down, then
it will briefly strongly pull up, before the open drain mode is applied.
Conversely, if the mode is applied before the level, and the pin
happened to be in input mode, with the unused "output value" being low,
then the pin will briefly strongly pull down, before being released.

It is desirable to avoid such glitches.  This CL lays the foundation for
that, by adding the means to simultaneously tell the transport backend
that the mode, output level, and weak pull mode needs to be modified.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I552016571af525cdb872f98abaf915c64ed57563

subject: [opentitantool] Use PullMode instead of WeakPushPull
body:
The output pins of HyperDebug or simulated "environment" can be employ
strong drive, either push/pull or open drain, and separately can enable
weak pullup / pulldown in case the strong drive is not active (e.g. when
output level is high, and the mode is "open drain", or when the pin mode
is "input".)

These options should be enough to simulate all weak and strong
strappings, provided that Toshak's claim that HyperDebug "weak" pull is
going to be weaker than the weak pull of the future OpenTitan ASIC
holds.  But for now, we can make sure our host_emulation and verilator
environments behaves such that the weak pull of the simulated
environment is weaker than the simulated OpenTitan chip.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I6aeb8d52bbe92227695a7e24c4bab93f00f8570b

subject: [opentitantool] Convenience methods for HyperDebug transport
body:
The existing `execute_command()` invokes a callback for each line of
response received.  This would be an efficient way of handling megabytes
of data, without having to keep it all in memory at the same time.
However, most actual use cases expect a single line of output, and it is
cumbersome for each caller to have to count callbacks, and handle the
error cases of receving none or more than one.

This PR adds convenience methods to transport/hyperdebug for doing
textual request/response, when expecting no output, a single line of
output, or even a single line of output which matches a given regular
expression.  This way, the error cases can be centrally dealt with.

subject: [cryptolib, kmac] Fix CFG sticky bits in KMAC driver
body:
If one runs SHA-3 opertation after KMAC, then SHA-3 is not computed
correctly by the cryptolib KMAC driver. The issue is `kmac_en` bit of
CFG is never cleared, because each KMAC/SHA3 invocation assumes that
the bits of CFG needs to be preserved accross calls.

However, inherently, some bits of CFG are KMAC HWIP configuration type
and they are expected to live accross multiple calls (e.g.
`entropy_mode`). Few others might be updated at each call. The bits of
CFG that need to be reset are in particular `kmac_en`, `kstrength`,
`mode` and `sideload`. This PR should fix that.

Signed-off-by: Fatih Balli <fatihballi@google.com>

found so we can choose a suitable severity.

subject: [opentitantool] Consolidate GPIO declarations before applying
body:
Sometimes a pin may appear under several levels of aliases in multiple
configuration files, and one file may specify e.g. OpenDrain mode
without specifying a level, while anoter file specifies a default "high"
level, without mentioning the mode.  If such two declarations used
different names for the same pin, the existing code could end up
applying the level before the mode, which HyperDebug may object to.  (As
it rejects setting level on pins in input mode.)

This change makes it such that before applying any pin configuration,
all pin configurations ultimately referring to the same pin will be
"consolidated", such that mode, level and weak pull will all be applied
atomically.  This both prevents glitches on the signals, and prevents
the aforementioned HyperDebug issue.

Some other undesirable behavior is fixed along the way, such as
previously if two gpio entries in the same file mentioned the same pin
name, but with different configuration, the latter would silently
override the former.  Doing the same now will cause an error (unless the
configurations are "compatible").

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>

subject: [spid] Passthrough to support CPOL 1
body:
_Related Issue: https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/16339 _

Previously, passthrough logic had a bug when CPOL is 1. When SCK is
inverted, meaning that the SCK remains high when CSb is de-asserted, the
filtering logic did not behave correctly.

The reason is the clock gating cell. To filter out the current command,
passthrough logic gates the output clock then delays the CSb and
release the CSb. The clock enable signal drops when the command needs to
be filtered. The logic sets the enable signal when CSb is released.

However, if CPOL is 1, then setting the enable signal enables the SCK at
the next low period of SCK, which is the beginning of the next
transaction. So, the next transaction misses one clock edge.

This commit tries to address the issue by:

1. Adding inverter in front of/ and at the end of the CG cell
2. Adding a CG for inverted clock.
3. Adding a MUX between normal SCK and inverted SCK selected by CPOL

This solution adds 2x inverter and one AND delay onto the SCK path.

Signed-off-by: Eli Kim <eli@opentitan.org>

subject: [sram_ctrl] Fix RMW corner case when escalating
body:
If a global escalation request and a RMW transaction
come in at the same time, the RMW transaction will not
be able to complete even though the TL gate allows for
transactions that are already pending inside the device
to respond back (to make the bus behavior less erratic
for a better SW debug experience).

The reason for this is the write part of the RMW
transaction, since the scrambling device blocks
any transaction in case the keys have been invalidated
due to escalation.

This patch fixes this corner case by specifically
allowing pending writes to complete upon escalation.

The rationale is that a write won't give an attacker any
advantage, especially since the scrambling keys are already
clobbered at that point, and the TL gate is not accepting
any additional transactions from the bus.

Fixes #17064.

subject: [top/dv] Fix back propagation of non-lockstep inputs in lockstep test
body:
The input ports of the ibex_core module are defined as `logic` without
an explicit net type. According to the standard, simulation tools are
thus supposed to model these inputs using a `var` type. However, it
turns out that some tools collapse input ports into a single object to
reduce the number of assignments to improve simulation performance. As a
result, glitches inserted to inputs of the non-lockstep core may
propagate back and also change the input of the lockstep core. If this
happens, both cores are glitched simultaneously without any alerts
firing.

To avoid this, we also glitch the corresponding input of the
ibex_lockstep instance to the opposite value. The ibex_lockstep
instance is embedded inside prim_buf cells across which glitches don't
progagate back. Also, the delay lines are embedded inside the
ibex_lockstep instance. It's thus fine to apply the glitch
simultaneously.

subject: [opentitantool] Lock serial port before using
body:
By default Unix character devices can be opened by multiple processed
simultaneously.  For serial ports, that results in the arriving data to
be arbitratily divided between the multiple readers.  It is hard to
imagine a scenario on which that would be desirable.  When done by
accident, by e.g. forgetting about a `minicom` in the background, when
starting `opentitantool console`, the result could be that a few
characters seem to be "dropped" now and then (when really those few
characters appear in the background `minicom`), causing engineers to
waste time looking for loose cables, or firmware bugs, when none exist.

For that reason, programs such as `minicom` will attempt to atomically
create a file under `/var/lock`, to prevent multiple instances from
opening the same serial port.  (See specification of the exact file
format here:
https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/ch05s09.html )

Another terminal program, 'tio` (used by the author), uses the Linux
system call `flock()` on the serial device itself for the same
effect (with the unfortunate result that one `minicom` instance and one
`tio` intance could simultaneously open the same port.)

This CL makes OpenTitanTool BOTH use `/var/lock` and `flock()`, to
prevent accidentally opening the same serial port with `opentitantool
console` that is used by either other `opentitantool` instance, or by
`minicom` or `tio`.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I62861c230835991312664b43b493e3ec5f42c314

subject: [base] Correct error in declaring module ids
body:
The `status.h` module declared `kStatusModuleId` as an global and intended
users to use `DECLARE_MODULE_ID` to create a local override with `static`
scope that would shadow the global.  Embarrassingly, I never wrote an
explicit test for this override behavior and the compiler complains
that a variable cannot be declared both `extern` and `static`.

In order to permit this shadowing behavior, I've updated the code to
name the default module ID as:
```
extern const uint32_t MODULE_ID;
```

and then permit users to `#define` their own MODULE_IDs to provide the
relevant constant (preprocessor substitutions always win):

```
 #define MODULE_ID MAKE_MODULE_ID('a', 'b', 'c')
```

subject: [entropy_src] Don't push to input FIFO unless indicating ready to AST
body:
In lowRISC/OpenTitan#16732 we started registering the rng_enable output
to AST to make the signal glitch free for closing CDC. As a result of
the introduced register, it became now possible for entropy_src to
push entropy from AST into the input FIFO despite indicating not being
ready. While this might not have been a big issue for the actual chip,
it led to large amount of failures in block-level DV due to the
push-pull agent on the AST interface, the scoreboard and the RTL
becoming out of sync whenever re-enabling entropy_src while AST provided
valid input data.

This can be fixed by only pushing valid data from AST into the input
FIFO if entropy_src is indeed indicating ready to AST. The behavior
during disabling of entropy_src isn't affected by this fix.

This resolves lowRISC/OpenTitan#17236.

IOC0 IOC1`, then do whatever to stimulate some action of the device
under test, and finally run `opentitantool gpio monitoring read IOC0
IOC1` to get a list of events such as "rising edge on IOC1 at such and
such time", "falling edge on ... at ...", ...

queued. Overflow will be reported by `monitoring read`.

monitoring read IOC0 IOC1 --continue` can be used, which must be
followed by another call to `monitoring read` (which could again

body:

`hw/ip` that has a `data/<name>.hjson` file except `trial1`.

This name is intended for use in titles and sentences of documentation.
Each name was thus chosen such that it:
1. is unique among the names of all hardware blocks in OpenTitan (e.g.,
   'SPI' alone is not sufficient when there is an SPI device and an SPI
   host and those are two different blocks);
2. is sufficient for referring to the hardware block without requiring a
   companion word (e.g., 'OpenTitan Big Number' does not work because it
   cannot be used in a sentence without a companion word: "[...] can be
   used on the OpenTitan Big Number [accelerator/hardware block/IP?]" --
   we want to avoid this ambiguity);
3. is concrete rather than abstract, because the name identifies a
   concrete hardware block which implements a specification and it does
   not identify the specification in general (e.g., 'AES' alone is not
   suitable because it identifies an algorithm/specification);
4. is close to the name of the module in code, which is the value of the
   `name` field (e.g., 'ADC Controller' is closer to `adc_ctrl` than
   'ADC Control Interface');
5. contains acronyms only if we expect those acronyms to be widely known
   in the industry (e.g., AES, I2C, SPI, or UART, but not CSRNG or EDN),
   because readers who are not familiar with this project should be able
   to get an idea of a hardware block from its name (also see footnote
   1).

This commit also updates the one-line and one-paragraph descriptions of
a hardware block to align them with the name (also see footnote 2).  We
capitalize the name in sentences exactly as in the `human_name` field to
emphasize that it is not just a noun but the name of a specific hardware
block.  As such, we use the name without articles (neither definite
'the' nor indefinite 'a'/'an') and without companion words (e.g.,
'hardware block' or 'IP').  (If it helps you, imagine the hardware block
that you're referring to as a person.)

For blocks that have their `.hjson` generated from a template
(`.hjson.tpl`), this commit updates the template and the generated
`.hjson`.  This commit also updates the `.hjson`s of the
top-level-specific blocks.

The new field that contains the human-readable name, `human_name`, is
added to `util/reggen` as optional.

Footnotes:
1. In the future, we may add a separate, optional field that defines an
   acronym that can be used to identify to a hardware block in contexts
   where readers are already somewhat familiar with the block.
2. Updating *all* documents to uniformly use the agreed names is out of
   scope of this commit, but we strongly encourage using them as
   described above in all new text.  We expect we'll update existing
   documents over time.

subject: [opentitantool] End session when parent process terminates
body:
The `opentitansession` can work as a daemon that connects to a backend
transport, and then detaches from the foreground terminal, as other unix
daemons.  The daemon can be told to stop by a signal.  This is useful at
times.

At other times, if one is writing a script for instance, which wants to
start the daemon at the top of the script, and keep it alive while the
script runs, it is not always convenient to ensure that if the script
terminates in abnormal ways, that it remembers to send a signal to the
`opentitansession` daemon.

This PR introduces a `--foreground` mode, which causes
`opentitansession` to not detach from the controlling terminal, and keep
running only as long as its parent process is alive.

Unfortunately, the Linux `prctl()` syscall is not part of the Rust `nix`
crate, so a bit of unsafe C linking of was necessary.

subject: [opentitantool] Propagate `transport init` to backend
body:
The existing command `opentitantool transport init` will send a series
of instructions to the backend to configure pins according to a set of
configuration files.  Ideally, that would bring the transport into a
known state.  However, sometimes the configuration is under-specified,
that is, maybe it omits declaring the direction of a pin as "Input",
relying on that being the default for all pins at power-on.  Doing so
opens up the possibility that if the debugger device has previously been
used with a different configuration file, which used the same pin as
output, then after `transport init` the pin would remain an output, to
the surprise of automated tests or operators.

This PR makes `transport init` first tell the backend transport to reset
to power-on state, before sending the usual series of pin-specific
instructions, hopefully reducing the risk of surprises.

Some backends, such as UltraDebug, do not support re-configuraion of
pin direction, and others, such as Verilator, do not have backend
hardware which could carry over state from one test to the next, so a
default empty implementation of the new method is provided.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>

subject: [doc] Replaced Hugo links with standard markdown
body:
A script, `util/check_links.py`, was written by Amaury
to automate most of the relinking.

Below are the commands run to perform the relinking.
Some moves had to be manually added to the move list,
because they were either not properly tracked by git
or to fix quirky behaviour of the script.

Note that command has to be run twice
because it can't handle non-bijective moves
and that it incorrectly re-links two files,
which are fixed in the final file.

```
git show --name-status HEAD~11..HEAD | grep '^R100' | sed 's/^R100\t//' > move_list.txt
echo "hw/dv/sv/dv_utils/doc/index.md hw/dv/sv/dv_utils/README.md" >> move_list.txt
echo "hw/dv/tools/doc/index.md hw/dv/tools/README.md" >> move_list.txt
echo "README.md doc/introduction.md" >> move_list.txt
echo "doc/project/checklist.md doc/project_governance/checklist/README.md" >> move_list.txt
./util/check_links.py . --ignore-book --move-list-file move_list.txt --apply

echo "hw/dv/tools/README.md util/dvsim/README.md" > move_list.txt
./util/check_links.py . --ignore-book --move-list-file move_list.txt --apply
git checkout HEAD -- SUMMARY.md hw/doc/cores.md
```

subject: [flash_ctrl] update `IPoly` parameter in flash scrambler
body:

for the flash scrambling scheme was not the Conway polynomial with
degree 64, but rather the Conway polynomial with degree 32.

After discussion in #17443, it was determined that while OK, as the
polynomial was still irreducible, a better, NIST recommended polynomial
should be used instead.

This updates the GF(2) irreducible polynomial used by the flash
scrambler to the NIST recommended polynomial for block ciphers:
`x^64 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1`.

subject: [opentitantool] Eeprom primitives in Spi trait
body:
This PR introduces a new method on the spi::Target trait, for doing SPI
transactions following the EEPROM format, that is, consisting of a few
bytes of command/address, followed by a chuck of data to be either read
or written, optionally followed by repeated polling a status bit, to see
if the operation is complete.

A default implementation of the new method is provided for transport
backends which support generic SPI read/write transactions, in effect
moving part of the code from the existing SpiFlash struct into the
spi::Target trait.

Going forward, transports that do not implement generic SPI
transactions, but supports only EEPROM/Flash-style protocol, can provide
their own implementation of the new trait method, and leave the existing
generic Spi transaction method either unimplemented, or severely
restricted.

subject: [opentitantool]: Proxy forwarding of strappings
body:
When using `opentitansession`, often the session process will be
provided with configuration files on startup, and the individual
`opentitantool` invocation may or may not get any configuration file
arguments.

To handle all cases, `gpio apply` should check if either the session
process knows a strapping by the name, and in that case have the session
process apply it, or check if local files declare a strapping by the
name, and in that case instruct the session process to individually
configure every pin mentioned in the strapping.

subject: [crypto] Fix completion check of Generate command
body:
The Generate command is complete only after all entropy bits have been
delivered.  In that case, we cannot poll the `cs_cmd_req_done` bit in
the `csrng_send_app_cmd` function because that will block software from
consuming entropy and thus block CSRNG from delivering all entropy bits,
which would cause a deadlock.  Instead, we poll the `genbits_vld` bit,
which rises as soon as entropy is available, and then return from
`csrng_send_app_cmd` when it was called for a Generate command.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [crypto] Fix usage of `csrng_send_app_cmd` for EDN
body:
Since 5cbddc36d85756fbe86f2a615717881292405c83 (PR #17350), the
`csrng_send_app_cmd` function is additionally being used to write EDN
registers that interface CSRNG in hardware.  In that use case, CSRNG's
SW status register cannot be used to check the status of a command, but
`csrng_send_app_cmd` unconditionally did so, which caused hangs.

This commit adds an argument, `check_completion`, to
`csrng_send_app_cmd` with which the checks can be disabled when the
function is called to write EDN registers.

interface, and uses a default configuration file depending on the

subject: [otbn, rtl] Blank flag generation in bignum ALU for SCA hardening
body:
Previously, there was a chance that transient effects between flags (in
particular MSB and LSB flags for logical operations) belonging to
different instructions could result in undesirable SCA leakage.

To prevent this, this commit blanks the data paths relevant for
managing and using the flags inside the bignum ALU similar to what is
done for the RF write data path. There are however two notable
exceptions where blanking cannot be applied without impacting the
performance of the architecture:
- Whether the Z flag for MAC operations is updated depends on the
  result of the MAC operation itself. This can result in SCA leakage
  related to previous Z flags. This commit slightly improves the
  situation by removing potential SCA leakage related to previous Z flag
  values of the other flag group.
- The BN.SEL selects either the data on read port A or B of the register
  file based on a single flag of one of the two flag groups. Even though
  flag selection is now blanked, there may be SCA leakage between the RF
  read ports as the flag selection result which serves as a selector
  input for the actual data is generated in the same pipeline stage.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

subject: [otbn, rtl] Improve blanking of flags, move clearing to predecoder
body:
Previously, the `operation_commit_i` input was evaluated to determine
when to not update and/or clear the flags. However, as this signal
factors in many combinatorial error signals from the controller, the
signal is most likely very glitchy which is bad for blanking/SCA hard-
ening. Therefore this commit stops using this signal in the flag
generation/updating logic and migrates the corresponding functionality
to the instruction fetch/predecoder stage.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

subject: [opentitantool] Only do UART pacing when SW flow control enabled
body:
In order for SW flow control to work, we cannot allow very many
characters to accumulate in buffers/FIFOs of the operating system or
hardware debuggers.  For that reason, the current code "paces" its
output, to ensure that there cannot be any built-up.

The overhead of such pacing may reduce the throughput, depending on
timer precision and system load.  The effect is large enough that the
Ti50 serial "rescue" bootstrapping takes 5 minutes instead of around 1
minute, which causes timeouts in automated tests.

This PR disables the pacing of the output, of software flow control is
disabled.  There can be no use cases for pacing without flow control, as
it could allow continuous output of characters at maximum speed,
assuming optimal timer behavior.  It cannot be "worse" than that without
pacing.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>

on the scb side.

subject: [entropy_src] Clarify different modes of operation (FIPS / FW_OV etc.)
body:
This commit adds quite some clarifications in the documentations and the
RTL (in the form of comments) related to the different modes of
operation of the ENTROPY_SRC block.

In particular, this commit:
- Unifies terminology to distinguish between FIPS/CC compliant mode
  (short FIPS mode) and boot-time / bypass mode. The term "normal mode"
  is now gone.
- Adds a new section to the programmers guide outlining how the
  different firmware override modes (observe vs. extract and insert),
  and they hardware conditioning bypass mode, and the entropy output
  reading mode can be enabled, how they relate to each other, and what
  the prerequisites are.
- Adds comments to the RTL to explain how entropy bits flow between the
  various FIFOs depending on which modes are configured.
- Aligns the theory of operation section with the newly created section
  in the programmers guide (the theory of operation section is at a
  much higher level) and removes some outdated information (e.g.
  regarding the ability to completely disable boot-time mode, and where
  entropy bits are read from in firmware override mode).
- Unifies the usage of kMultiBitBool4False/True instead of a mix of
  these and MuBi4True/False Mubi4 False etc.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#17408.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

subject: [entropy_src] Don't predict counter clearing in FW_OV mode, align doc
body:
Previously, the scoreboard was assuming that even in FW_OV mode (extract
and insert) the health test failure counters would be cleared upon full
passing test sequences. But this is not right. In FW_OV mode those
counters are not cleared as firmware may want to observe those values
when working on the extracted entropy bits (during that time further
entropy might be collected which is discarded and should not lead to
a clearing of the failure counters).

This hasn't been explicitly documented yet but the main FSM
(entropy_src_main_sm.sv) contains a comment on that:

"Even when stalled we keep monitoring for alerts and maintaining alert
 statistics. However, we don't signal alerts or clear HT stats in FW_OV
 mode."

Therefore, this commit aligns DV and doc with the RTL implementation.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

subject: [opentitantool] Do not convert line endings in opentitantool
body:
Serial output from an embedded microcontroller is often used for
debugging.  In production systems, connection would typically require
something like a FTDI device, to pick up the TTL-level UART output, and
present it in a way that `minicom` or similar can access through
`/dev/ttyUSBn`.

If used as above, it is important that the microcontroller outputs
`"\r\n"` line terminators, in order for minicom to do both carriage return
and newline.

Given that the firmware should already output that two-character
sequence, there is no point in having opentitantool convert `"\n"` into
`"\r\n"`.  In fact, doing so i counter-productive, in that it causes
`"\r\r\n"`, which is at best harmless, but at worst causes undesired
empty lines, or mangles up binary communication piped through
`opentitantool console`.  (Googlers, see b/255397131)

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: Icff368780634089a9c9b3b5bd7c02f2f461a9435

subject: [opentitantool] Add Dediprog backend
body:
SPI support for Dediprog, it is able to program firmware into a CW310
and, and read from an EEPROM chip.

The voltage level of Dediprog is exposed as a GPIO pin "VCC", which is
permanently in AnalogOutput mode.

The driver suffers from not being able to read IO levels, voltage, or
SPI clock speed from the device, only set it.  So every time the driver
is initialized, it will reset to default values.

For the reasons above, the drivers initial VCC voltage is zero
volts (disabled).  The default `dediprog.json` declares 3.5 volt, which
gets applied by `transport init`.  Each command line invocation of
opentitantool will re-set the driver state, so all commands including
`transport init` must be given in a single invocation, e.g.:
```
opentitantool --interface=dediprog --exec 'transport init' bootstrap ...
```

Using `opentitansession` will mitigate the above issues, as the session
daemon will keep the driver open, and "remember" the values of GPIO pins
and current voltage/speed.  The same is the case for Rust programs that
directly use opentitanlib.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I275a514dff0086f3e1b3449a9bf2002bb8e3f00e

subject: [opentitantool] Improved emulator startup
body:
Rather than having the host emulation sub-process connect to a socket of
the parent process, as means of confirming successful startup, instead
rely on standard output from sub-process.

This has the advantage that if the sub-process crashes, and will never
acknowledge, no timeout is needed, as unlike with listening on a socket,
the parent process cannot avoid noticing the standard output pipe of the
child process being closed.

subject: [opentitantool] Improve host emulation process termination
body:
If the sub-process does not respond to SIGTERM for five seconds, the
code will attempt SIGKILL, which is sensible.

The code attempts to detect whether the repeated SIGKILL attempts have
worked, by checking if we get a ESRCH (no such process) from the
`signal()` system call.  However, it seems that doing that may not be a
reliable way of detecting termination, possibly because a process in
zombie state still counts as "existing" in the eyes of `signal()`.

This CL adapts the code to call `waitpid()` in between calls to
`signal()`, in order to check if the sub-process has terminated.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I4ec30d7bb99e56ca4c21b0390e3cec6660f3dde8

subject: [csrng/rtl] Fix `cs_aes_halt_ack` for four-phase HS
body:
The `cs_aes_halt` interface follows a four-phase handshake protocol.
This implies that `ack` does not drop before `req`.  The current CSRNG
code, which originated from #10830, violates this condition.  This
commit fixes that.

This will be made visible in DV with the subsequent commit.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [csrng/dv] Use four-phase HS for `cs_aes_halt`
body:
Prior to this commit, the request signal of `cs_aes_halt`, which gets
driven by a DV agent, would drop as soon as CSRNG had set acknowledge
high for a single cycle.  This does not correspond to how `entropy_src`,
which usually drives the request signal, would necessarily behave.
Instead, `entropy_src` could keep the request asserted for many cycles
after CSRNG has acknowledged it.

By changing the agent to a four-phase handshake, the agent can now also
keep the request high after the acknowledge.  This would expose the bug
fixed by the previous commit.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [sca, fpga] Increase start trigger delay for AES and KMAC peripherals
body:
During FPGA measurements we have been observing stability issues with
the power rails for fixed vs. random TVLA. In some cases, loading the
fixed plaintext/key discharges the power rails slightly more or less
than loading random plaintexts/keys, which then leads to a vertical
offset in the traces and thus "fake" leakage unrelated to the actual
processing. Increasing the start trigger delay allows the power rails to
recharge before the actual processing phase to be analyzed starts.

subject: [openocd/rv_dm] Workaround rv_dm bug in OpenOCD by retrying failed commands
body:
See issue #18087 for more details. In short, this commits works around the
problem by detecting when a DMI operations fails, wait for the DM/DMI to
get unstuck, reset the DMI and retry. It logs an ERROR so that problem does
not go unoticed.

The "DMI is stuck" condition is easily detectable because by requesting a
DMI reset, we get back the current value of DTMCS. This value is (per spec
and per implementation) always of the form 0x0000xyzt. When stuck, we will
get 0xffffffff which is clearly invalid. When that happens, we continue
issuing DMI resets until we see something different.

At the moment, and it is unclear why, we never get "partly invalid" values,
ie we either get a correct DTMCS value or 0xffffffff which is why the
detection above works. If it turns out that this assumption is wrong,
this patch might fail to detect the problem.

Signed-off-by: Amaury Pouly <amaury.pouly@lowrisc.org>

subject: [csrng, rtl] Simplify main input mux
body:
Previously, this main entropy mux had multiple all-zero inputs that were
not actually required from a functionality perspective. The only case
where the design needs the input to be really zero is when flag0 is set.

This commit thus implements the following changes to the mux:
1. Reduce the number of all-zero inputs (lower FI attack surface). The
   only all-zero input is when the FI-hardened flag0 field is set.
2. Only flop new input from entropy source if an entropy request is
   actually outstanding. Previously, a glitch on the acknowledge line
   would have caused CSRNG to flop whatever was on the bus (it wouldn't
   necessarily have been consumed downstream though).

This resolves lowRISC/OpenTitan#16564.

outputting a deterministic value such as 0 after read may open FI
attack windows. This is especially true as we have countermeasures
in various places in the entropy complex (e.g. at the input of CSRNG)
to check that the entropy source doesn't deliver the same word twice in
a row. However, these countermeasures don't detect if an adversary
managed to latch a single all zero seed into CSRNG which may result
in fully deterministic CSRNG output.

This is inline with lowRISC/OpenTitan#9261 and lowRISC/OpenTitan#5341

unnecessary reads and writes to the `uint32_t *ctx` parameter.

without hardware conditioning. This requires the bypass/boot-time health
test window size to be configured to 384 bits. Other window sizes are
not tested and also not supported at the moment. The same restriction
applies to the non-boot-time bypass mode, i.e., if ES_ROUTE and ES_TYPE
are both set to True.

This workaround took the device out of `BOOTSTRAP_RMA` and delayed for a little
while to enable transitions into RMA. This was necessary because OTBN was not
ready for RMA while in the spin loop that the `BOOTSTRAP_RMA` strapping creates.

transition to RMA while in the `BOOTSTRAP_RMA` strapping. This commit removes
the workaround.

not enough to connect and transition within.

subject: [lc_ctrl] SVA fix in kmac interface
body:
This removes the first prim_sync_reqack_data instance
and just directly connects the token data bus to the
kmac domain.

This is done to fix a simulation issue with CDC instrumentation
enabled. I.e., due to the use of two prim_sync_reqack_data
instances, it can happen that the handshake has already
completed on the first one, but not on the second one.

This causes these two primitives to not operate in tandem anymore,
and can trip the SyncReqAckHoldReq assertion in the first primitive.

We can safely remove the first instance, since that instance does
not contain a data register (the data is guaranteed to remain stable
throughout the kmac operation).

subject: [sw/silicon_creator] Add structured kChipInfo to ROM
body:
This commit adds a new `chip_info_t` struct that contains info about the
ROM's provenance. The ROM now prints the Git commit hash on shutdown
after the "VER:" prefix.

The ROM linker script was already configured to place the .chip_info
section at the top of ROM, but I'm not confident that it worked as
expected. The autogenerated header contained a static constant, so I
think a copy would be inlined at some arbitrary location into any
compilation unit that used it, rather than being placed by the linker
script.

To verify that the ROM prints the Git commit hash on shutdown:

    ./bazelisk.sh test --test_output=streamed \
      //sw/device/silicon_creator/rom/e2e:shutdown_output_dev_fpga_cw310_rom

To verify that the .chip_info section contains data from chip_info.o:

    ./bazelisk.sh build-then 'less %s' --config riscv32 \
      //sw/device/silicon_creator/rom:rom_with_fake_keys_fpga_cw310_map

To see the value of `kChipInfo` at the end of ROM:

    ./bazelisk.sh build-then 'xxd %s | less' --config riscv32 \
      //sw/device/silicon_creator/rom:rom_with_fake_keys_fpga_cw310_bin

For example, here's the end of the ROM from the previous command. At
0x7f80, there are 64 bits of a Git commit hash (e20871e1cf102bf6).

    00007f70: 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000  ................
    00007f80: f62b 10cf e171 08e2                      .+...q..

Issue #14892

subject: [opentitantool] Recovery from failed HyperDebug firmware update
body:
The Ti50 team plans a test lab, with hands-off HyperDebug devices
connected to OpenTitan as well as previous generation security chips.

As the first thing, before running a test suite, our script currently
runs: `opentitantool --interface hyperdebug transport update-firmware`,
which ensures that the firmware version of the debugger matches the
current version of opentitantool.  (opentitantool will only rarely be
updated, but it is cheap to perform the `update-firmware` as it skips if
the USB version string of HyperDebug already matches.)

We have become aware of a possible error case, if the update process is
interrupted, then HyperDebug will remain in the DFU bootloader mode,
meaning that it presents itself with alternative USB VID:DID, resulting
in `--interface hyperdebug` not recognising the device.  We do not want
to always have the backend driver accept the DFU identification, as the
debugger would not be able to do any of the usual operations.  However,
when asked to update firmware, it would be desirable that
`opentitantool` would accept either VID:DID.

Already, the special-purpose backend driver `--interface hyperdebug_dfu`
exists, and accepts only the DFU bootloader identification, this can be
used to recover a HyperDebug in DFU mode.  However, in order to keep our
scripts simple, with this PR I propose to have `hyperdebug_dfu` accept
either the normal or the DFU USB identification, allowing our script to
run: `opentitantool --interface hyperdebug_dfu transport
update-firmware` and be confident that it will work both in the happy
case, as well as when HyperDebug was previously left in DFU mode.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: Ic27134f5ace917bcbe2672ce7d705e3f9d27673b

subject: [opentitantool] Allow not running image immediately after bootstrap
body:
Sometimes automated tests want to set up serial ports, GPIO edge
detection, etc. before booting a firmware image under test.  The
bootstrapping protocol may itself use some of the same pins, meaning
that some time after completed bootstrap could pass, before the testing
infrastructure is ready to observe the startup behavior of the firmware.
Also, the firmware in question could read and modify persistent storage
on the chip, meaning that it is undesirable to have it execute
immediately after completed bootstrapping, only to have to reset it
again, while the testing infrastructure gets ready for the "real" test
run.

This PR adds an option to have `opentitantool bootstrap` perform its
logic, but leave the RESET pin asserted in the end (as it is removing
strappings, etc.).  This will allow the testing infrastructur to first load
the firmware image to be tested, and then take its sweet time to set up
whatever pins and ports, before eventually releasing the chip from
reset.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I1762abf437d3eebf8215127dd5463f69d3b1e8d4

subject: [csrng/rtl] Restrict `glen` to 12 bit (thus <= 4095)
body:
Prior to this commit, the `glen` field, which defines the number of
128-bit entropy block each Generate command returns, had a width of 13
bit (`[24:12]`) and thus took a maximum value of 2^13 - 1 = 8191.  This
is problematic because it would have led CSRNG to return up to 8191 *
128 bit, which is larger than the maximum number of bit per request
allowed by NIST (2^19) bit, for one Generate command (#18334).

This commit reduces the width of the `glen` field to 12 bit, so that its
maximum value is now 4095, thereby reducing the upper bound of bit per
request below the maximum stipulated by NIST.  This commit thus resolves
the HW part of #18334.

The upper bound is now 128 bit lower than the allowed maximum, which
could have been avoided if the `glen` field was kept at a width of 13
bit and CSRNG instead checked its value and returned an error if it
exceeded 2^12.  Such an error response mechanism is currently not
implemented, however, and implementing one from scratch was out of scope
for this change.

This change was tested by setting `glen` to 4095 in `csrng_smoke_test`;
the test passed and a manual inspection of the waves looked correct.
This change was further tested with a full block-level regression run,
although randomization of `glen` is currently limited to the range
[1:32]; this will be resolved separately (due to deadline constraints).

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [aes, sw, sca] Use separate software LFSR for key masking
body:
Previously, we were using the same software PRNG used for generating
plaintexts and keys. This was non-ideal for the following reasons:
1. One must be careful to keep the software PRNG on the target and the
   host in sync. Not only can this be difficult but it also limits
   capture performance on the host side.
2. This PRNG is not available in non-batch mode. As a result, non-batch
   mode was always using unmasked keys which led to 1st-order leakage.

Therefore, this PR uses an additional software LFSR for key masking
(similar to what is done for KMAC already) including a simple serial
command to seed that LFSR. Key re-masking can still be disabled by
seeding this LFSR with 0.

subject: [opentitantool] "provides"/"requires" in configuration files
body:
Often `opentitantool` will be used with multiple configuration files.
That is one configuration file will define how the pins of the chip
under test are connected to e.g. HyperDebug pins, such as "IOR11" being
an alias of "CN9_26".  Another configuration file may define the use of
various pins by the firmware image currently being run, e.g. that
"LID_OPEN" is an alias of "IOR11", and that it should be in open-drain
mode, defaulting to being driven low by HyperDebug.  This latter file
relies on opentitantool already knowing about a pin called "IOR11".

At Google, we will use opentitantool for other security chips besides
OpenTitan, and it is important that configuration files belonging to
distinct test setups are not accidentally mixed.  Currently, such
mis-configuration will typically be discovered by means of an error such
as "No such pin: IOR11", which may confuse the test writer, who does not
see IOR11 anywhere in his script, only LID_OPEN.

In order detect such errors before the script even starts, and be able
to print more meaningful error messages, the feature introduced in this
PR will allow the first of the above files do declare `provides: { "chip":
"opentitan" }`, while the second file would declare `requires: { "chip":
"opentitan" }`.  That trying to use the second file without the first,
or with a different chip altogether, would then result in an immediate
error message `Expected value "opentitan" for key "chip", found "..."`.

This feature will also be useful by allowing test scripts to branch
depending on what the various testbed can support, as declared in
configuration files.  If for instance the long cables of CW310 inteferes
with 1MHz I2C communication, while the future PCB with ASIC will support
fast communication, we could choose to declare `provides: {
"i2c_speed_limit": "400000" }` for the former, and then the test script
can run `opentitantool transport query i2c_speed_limit`, and branch
depending on the output.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: Ia5ccf9dd9e6183c11185a22f122e2f9a3f9451cc

subject: [aes, rtl] Update S-Box data/mask in sync with PRD
body:
Previously, it was possible that DOM S-Box instances would get new data
and mask inputs without receiving new PRD / updating the internally
buffered PRD which is not ideal from an SCA perspective. Even if the
S-Box isn't evaluated this may create SCA leakage in the first
multiplier stage.

This commit modifies the design as follows:
- A new input is added to the DOM S-Box to directly control the
  internal PRD buffering. Upon writing state / key registers also
  the buffering is now updated.
- Inside the key expand module, some signals are added to inhibit or
  enforce PRD buffer updates irrespective of key register updates
  because some operation modes require this.

With these changes, the non-linear logic inside the S-Boxes is always
presented with both fresh data/masks and PRD except for the following
special cases:
- Key expand module: Switching betweeen FWD and INV mode of operation,
  e.g. for decryption key generation and upon switching configuration
  (rare).
- Data path: The very first cycle of the initial round for encryptions
  and decryptions. This is not critical as in the initial round the
  masked plaintext/ciphertext (not secret) is presented to the S-Boxes
  but the S-Boxes aren't evaluated.

subject: [e2e tests] Do not use SRST in OpenOCD reset configuration.
body:
Andreas has identified that OpenOCD was configured to use SRST
when issue a `reset`  command. This is problematic since it resets
the entire chip, including the JTAG tap and the pinmux.
This then causes the pinmux to disable the connection between the pins
and the tap a bit later and most likely causes the JTAG issues identified
in #17729.
The real chip will not have a srst_n pin and it should not be needed because
on RISC-V, issuing a DMI reset though ndmreset will reset *everything* but
the part necessary to keep the jtag tap alive, which is exactly what we want.

Note that the GDB tests never need to reset the entire chip, this is only needed
for LC transitions which are done in separate tests using opentitanlib and not
GDB, and that correctly handle this detail.

Hopefully fixes #17729.

Signed-off-by: Amaury Pouly <amaury.pouly@lowrisc.org>

subject: [opentitantool] Speed up HyperDebug driver
body:
Avoid waiting for serial timeout on every HyperDebug console command.
This is achieved by stopping the processing immediately, when the
command prompt "\n> " is detected at the trailing end of characters
received from `read()` (rather than doing another `read()` with 10ms
timeout after that, and only stopping if that came back without any
characters.)

Also, rather than purging any spurious output before sending the
command, it is now done after sending the command, using the echo of the
command just sent to recognize when to start processing.  (Betting that
the probability of seeing the same command as part of the spurious
output will be vanishing, as that would otherwise cause the rest of the
spurious output to be incorrectly treated as ligitimate command output.)

This change reduces the time of `transport init` from 4.6s to 1.1s for
the Ti50 team, which would significantly speed up automated test runs.
(Currently, the actual test logic can sometimes be faster than the
setup.)

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: Iea26da31676ab5607b46b644870454b52dd4eb1a

subject: [sdc] Add draft of SPI constraints
body:
Four sets of SPI constraints are included here, corresponding to
different modes:
1. spi_device generating responses internally for 48 MHz full-cycle
   sampling (flash mode or generic mode)
2. spi_device generating responses internally for 24 MHz half-cycle
   sampling (TPM mode, typically)
3. spi_device passthrough for 33 MHz full-cycle sampling
4. spi_host performing full-cycle sampling

All constraints are timed for SPI mode 0.
For spi_device operation with CSB from the DIO, SPI_DEV_CS_L is promoted
to a clock. This makes for awkward constraints where it is used as data
or a reset, so the paths will need to be audited to ensure the behavior
matches expectations.

subject: [opentitantool] Avoid no-op HyperDebug firmware updates
body:
The special flag `--interface hyperdebug_dfu` allows opentitantool to
recognize a HyperDebug deview whether it is in its normal mode or DFU
bootloader mode.  This is particularly useful when requesting firmware
update, as doing so can recover from previous interrupted update
attempts.

However, the logic to skip updating, in case the device is already
running the newest firmware version had been omitted from the
`hyperdebug_dfu` path, probably because the first incarnation of that
mode recognized only a board already in DFU mode, and hence special
purpose for developers or first-time users.

Now that `hyperdebug_dfu` should be used as the default for scripted
updating, we want it to recognize the common case, in which updating can
be skipped.  This PR adds logic for that.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>

subject: [i2c] Remove SCL glitch when FMT FIFO empties mid-transaction
body:
Prior to this change, if the FMT FIFO doesn't yet have its next entry
from software and the transaction is not done (i.e. STOP hasn't been
issued), the i2c FSM would cause a glitch on SCL. The FSM would follow
the sequence HostHoldBitAck -> PopFmtFifo -> Idle, and the Idle state
would unconditionally cause a 0 -> 1 transition on SCL, even if the user
intended to follow up with more data. Consequently, the host and device
would fall out of alignment for the bit count.

For the purposes of an ECO, change the Idle state to only release SCL if
it is not in the middle of a transaction in host mode. A subsequent
commit may change the FSM for readability (e.g. going to Active if this
IP is still in the middle of a bus transaction and fixing up the Active
state to wait for instructions from the FMT FIFO).

Signed-off-by: Alexander Williams <awill@opentitan.org>

subject: opentitantool: Allow instantiating emulation backend w/o executable
body:
The ordinary was to use the emulation backend is to start
opentitansession with it, giving an executable on the command line.  The
session process can then fork the emulation sub-process, and respond to
incoming network requests by manipulating the sub-process.

The test automation used by the Ti50 team wants to query each "testbed"
as part of test suite initialization, and that involves running
`opentitantool transport query` commands, which are meant to just return
values from the configuration files.  However, as the transport backend
is instantiated before the command is dispatched, the above command
currently fails for the host emulation backend.  As the very
initialiation of the backend attempts to fork a sub-process, without
having the name of the executable to start.

This CL makes the setup routine (`get_configuration()`) recognize when
no executable is given, and skip its operation.  (Should the user
attempt to start the emulation, an error will be reported by
`spawn_process()`.)  This change allows the `opentitantool transport
query` command to complete.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I3209d4e9bfaec7bd68b85a58171e5c074faf11cf

- Remove scan mode paths from the SPI clocks. These paths are specific
  to a different mode, and they should use a different clock definition

- Relax hold constraints for the passthrough clock gates. Primarily,
  there were issues with the clock gate intended for CPOL=1, as it would
  do same-edge hold timing and fail, while the incoming data would
  actually launch on the other edge than the constraints indicated
  (because CPOL would be 1). Since we don't mind if the filter clips
  before the second-to-last can get through, the multicycle constraint
  that pushes back the hold / capture edge works well enough.
- Add missing multicycle constraint for SPI_DEV_PASS_IN_CLK to the
  output ports. Because this is modeling full-cycle sampling, the
  capture edge needs to be pushed back for setup.
- Add multicycle constraint for CSB as TPM reset. Because a CSB edge
  cannot coexist with a SPI_TPM_CLK edge, the hold time requirement is

 transaction in case the device returns a nak in the addressing phase. This
 affects performance since the driver must wait the full transaction to

 This commit split the read into two transactions:

subject: [edn/dv] Fix state sampling loop in `edn_disable_vseq`
body:
When `edn_disable_vseq` should wait for a specific state of EDN's main
FSM, it has to sample the FSM state in every clock cycle.  To prevent
race conditions with events that change the FSM state, this ideally is
implemented with a `clocking` block, which we don't have in this case.
Alternatively, the DV env can sample signals of the DUT on the inactive
clock edge.

This commit changes the sampling of the main FSM state in
`edn_disable_vseq` to the negative clock edge.  It additionally changes
the loop from a `while` construct where the first value gets compared
before it gets sampled to a `forever` construct that does not have this
problem.  This commit also changes the wait statement in the other
branch of the surrounding `if`-`else` statement, so that both branches
are in-phase.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [edn/dv] Immediately disable EDN in `edn_disable_vseq`

complete means that this vseq never hits certain FSM states.  This can
be avoided by not waiting for outstanding CSR accesses and disabling EDN
through a backdoor write.

states.  Consequentially, these states are very seldomly hit by a purely
random delay.

This commit changes `edn_err_vseq` so that it awaits a random state of
Main FSM or Ack FSM (with a probability of 90%) before it inserts an
error that triggers an escalation that affects those FSMs.  This
substantially increases the coverage of the transition from each of

subject: [i2c/dv] Nullify CDC instrumentation effects on SCL and SDA
body:
Nullify the CDC instrumentation delays on the input synchronizers, since
SDA never truly changes simultaneously with SCL. Their happening on the
same cycle in simulation is due to time/cycle quantization.

For data, SDA *must* change after SCL is sampled as 0, so there is
always at least t_f_min between SCL change and SDA change. This may be
less than one IO_CLK_DIV4 cycle, but it should still be significantly
longer than any skew between the synchronizer paths (> 10 ns).

For START and STOP conditions, the setup and hold times for SDA changes
relative to SCL is at least 260 ns, far longer than any anticipated skew
between synchronizer paths.

for Bignum RF due to high resource consumption and this causes
leakage with FPGA experiments. This is an intermediate solution.
We are keeping shares in registers with higher Hamming distance

subject: [dv, key_sideload_agent] Fix DV environment hanging issue under reset
body:
Previously, the `get_and_drive()` task was consuming zero time when the
reset was active. This resulted in the key sideload interface endlessly
updating the sideload key and the whole DV environment to completely
hang. The root cause of this issue was the custom `wait_clks()`
implementation of the agent which 1) immediately returned when the reset
was active, and 2) was itself called in a forever loop consuming zero
time.

To fix this, this commit makes sure every iteration of forever loop
inside `get_and_drive()` takes at least one clock cycle. In line with
this change, the constraint for the response delay is adjusted to allow
for a minimum response delay of zero clock cycles (previously one). The
functions for waiting for clocks cycles and/or resets are copied over
from the clock and reset interface (`clk_rst_if.sv`) used in other
places of the project.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#19025.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

subject: [otbn, sca] Modify boolean_to_arithmetic routine against SCA
body:
This changes are done regarding to outcomes of the COCO-Alma
tool usage. Moreover, many more rules are put in the OTBN Security
Guidance Document. Please see it before developing algorithms
on OTBN which handle secret data.

If we don't have these changes, the tool reports there
are transient leakage and we may see leakage on the final
product even if we don't see a leakage on FPGA experiments.

We are also seeing a stable leakage on the MSB of the
intermediate values. We acknowledge that and since the
algorithm runs with 64-bit excess randomness, we don't
expect that to be possible to use that leakage and
retrieve secret values. We also verified that the stable
leakage disappeared after running the routine on 320-bit
instead of 321-bit.

commit. However, these changes fix things with 1.0.1 (the latest

guide the tool so that it knows what's going on. There's also a small

OTBN running and the task should complete when OTBN is still busy. The
idea is that we might want to e.g. inject an error into OTBN while
it's running.

There was a bug, and this code actually returned when OTBN was either
busy running something or was doing its end-of-run secure wipe. This
is weaker than callers of the task (otbn_rf_base_intg_err_vseq, for
example) might expect.

I only saw this at all because that sequence sometimes failed. It
turns out that its "guess a sensible time to stop" logic was sometimes
unlucky and guessed a time when OTBN doing its final secure wipe. The
rest sequence then wanted to inject an error on the register file, but
that didn't work: the register file wasn't used again!

subject: [usbdev,dv] Rename clocks in TB to fix various base tests
body:
Before this commit, we had two clocks in the testbench:

    usb_clk (48MHz)    : Wired to "clk_i"
    clk (faster)       : Wired to "clk_aon_i"

The problem was caused by the fact that "clk" was also used as the
main clk/rst interface. We've got various DV code that assumes this
main clock interface (accessible through cfg.clk_rst_vif) is the one
used for things like alert propagation.

In particular, we've got checks that make sure a fatal alert gets
re-asserted every 6 cycles. To count these cycles, we uses the "main
clock". Before this change, the "main clock" that we were tracking was
faster than the one that the prim_alert_sender was using, which meant
that the alert didn't get re-asserted quickly enough.

This commit renames things slightly so that we have an explicit
usb_clk and aon_clk, but the "main clock" of the device is now the
thing that got passed in as clk_i, so the alert checks described above
now work properly.

A separate problem with the testbench is that the usb clock is
currently configured to be slower than the AON clock, which is the
wrong way around. That relationship isn't changed by this commit, but
we'll fix it up to be more sensible in a followup.

Signed-off-by: Rupert Swarbrick <rswarbrick@lowrisc.org>

subject: [usbdev,dv] Fix speed of AON clock

This is backwards: it's supposed to be much slower (and low power!).
Switch the two around.

The real speed of the AON clock is going to be even slower than is
configured here, but having the two be reasonably similar should give
the same test efficacy and make the tests quicker to run (and debug!).

subject: [otbn,dv] Wait long enough for RF read in otbn_rf_base_intg_err_vseq

This vseq wants to start an OTBN run and then, at some time after the
run has started, corrupt the next read of the base register file. Of
course, this needs a bit of a wait: we need to wait until the base
register file is being read. This wait is usually very short (we read
from the RF with most instructions) but is rather longer if we happen
to be stalled reading from RND!

The stall for a RND read is longer when CDC is enabled, and pushed us
over the 2000 cycle max wait. Increasing by another multiple of 10
seems to fix things.

body:

compiler flags. Once the flags are in place, the aspect generates an
action that runs the clang-tidy wrapper script.

subject: [bazel] Rework module ID check rules to make the output more readable
body:
The way the current rule works, opentitantool is run on every elf files
and since it's a "build" step, the output will logged and printed by
bazel. This is not ideal since opentitantool likes to print messages
like a missing configuration files, which means that bazel will print
at least two lines *per test*. In case there is an actual error, the
output will be lost in a sea of useless messages. This commits reworks
the aspect rule to run a bash script that logs the opentitantool output
to a file. This output is not printed unless the module ID check fails.
This makes the output considerably smaller and will make CI output a lot
more useful.

subject: [crypto] Modify RSA to infer the size of signatures.
body:
Previously, the RSA signature code had separate `finalize()` functions
for each size of signature verification. Now, it will read the mode from
OTBN and infer the correct size. This provides more safety against size
mismatches and also an interface that better matches the top-level
cryptolib API.

This commit also modifies the key generation routine to double-check the

subject: [opentitantool] Improve UART on ti50 emulation
body:
Host emulation works by compiling the GSC code into a Linux executable,
instead of an image for OpenTitan, and running this executable as a
sub-process to `opentitansession`.

The sub-process will create a number of unix pipes, for UARTs and
other peripherals, and will use these to communicate with the simulation
environment.

Prior to this CL, `opentitantool console` would not capture the first
serial console output, because of a race.  The sub-process would create
the unix pipes, tell opentitansession that was is ready, and then
immediately proceed to produce output to the unix pipe representing the
serial console.  This allowed opentitansession no time to connect to the
pipe, and any data sent before a reading process has connected will be
lost.

This CL introduces a handshake, such that the sub-process is instructed
to wait after having indicated that it is done creating Unix pipes.
Also, opentitansession will now connect all UART pipes on sub-process
startup, rather than only at first read operation.  Together, these
changes allow the emulator to guarantee that the `opentitantool console`
will show the very first serial console output as the emulated chip
comes out of reset.

Signed-off-by: Jes B. Klinke <jbk@chromium.org>
Change-Id: I303ffe7f4f0ae39c1f6e26ba06a540b5898e063b

subject: [opentitantool] Fixes to the GSC rescue bootstrap protocol
body:
As an optimization, trailing pages of all FF bytes are not attempted
programmed.  It turns out a bug was triggered if the last page were not
all FF, and actually needed to be programmed.

This CL adresses it by properly padding the last block transmitted via
serial protocol with FFs, such that it does not trigger the bootloader
to attempt to program past the end of the image region.

subject: [sw/otbn/crypto] Add arithmetic to boolean masking for P256 ECDH
body:
This commit modifies the p256_scalar_mult function so that it returns
an arithmetically masked result. The arithmetic masking is done before
converting back to affine coordinates. For this the internal
scalar_mult_int function is changed to return projective coordinates.
The transformation to affine coordinates now needs to be done outside
scalar_mult_int.

This commit also adds code to convert from arithmetic masking to
boolean masking. The conversion is implemented following Gaubin's
algorithm to prevent side-channel leakage. The conversion is
implemented in a 257-bit domain to enable carry bit handling,
which is necessary when the arithmetic masking is performed
within a mod p domain.

Both described changes are then put together to generate the P256
ECDH shared session key.

Further, this commit also adds the relevant tests.

subject: [sw/otbn/crypto] Restructure P256 code to prevent IMEM overflow

an IMEM overflow. For this, p256.s is split into several individual
files containing different functions. In case the functions are not
needed for a specific binary, they now won't get inserted into the

subject: [sw/crypto] Hardening of P-384 implementation
body:
This commit includes the following changes:
- The internal scalar multiplication function now requires the scalar
value to be handed over as additive (modulo n) shares.
- Therefore, scalar k and private key d are now stored in shares in DMEM
- The shares are expanded by 64 bits to 448-bit values. This is a
side-channel protection measurement.
- Scalar and base point multiplication functions as well as the signing
function are adapted to the mentioned scalar/key handling.
- For signing the shares are masked multiplicatively to not reveal the
scalar/key value via side-channel leakage during signature computation.
- For multiplicative masking a new 448x128-bit multiplication function
is added, as well as a modular reduction function (modulo n).
- The mentioned changes increase code size quite significantly. Because
of this, (internal) scalar and base point multiplication are separated
into own source code files to prevent IMEM overflow.

Signed-off-by: Moritz Wettermann <moritz.wettermann@gi-de.com>

subject: [sw] Eliminate false positives from Clang-Tidy
body:
cfrantz@opentitan.org noticed that //quality:clang_tidy_check was
failing. It turns out that Clang-Tidy was generating false positives,
mostly about potentially uninitialized variables.

Brief timeline:

* In PR #18773, I temporarily removed Clang-Tidy's --warnings-as-errors
  flag until my work on C warning flags was complete (issue #12553).

* I attempted to fix these false positives in #18774 (never merged) by
  creating pure C definitions of the HARDENED* macros. That technique
  may have been workable, but it enabled the compiler to see through the
  analysis barrier for real builds, which would obviously be a problem.

* In PR #18719, I mistakenly brought back the --warnings-as-errors flag
  without fixing Clang-Tidy's false positives.

The main fix in this commit is to short-circuit the launder32() barrier
*only* when the code is built for static analysis. It also adds some
conditionally-compiled assertions to convince the analyzer that certain
pointers in memory.c are not NULL.

Closes #18774

subject: [bazel,manuf] Integrate platform transition in opentitan_binary
body:
At the moment, opentitan_binary produces a "<name>.elf" target
with a platform constraint but it uses cc_binary on which we
cannot define a transition. This means that any target that
depends on such an ELF file will not trigger a transition
and be built with the same platform (unless this rule defines
a transition on its attributes). This is problematic for tests
that needs to compile a tool with the host toolchain but build
some artefact with the platform toolchain, hence the use of
platform_target. This is not ideal though because the situation
protentially repeats with every binary built by opentitan_binary
so it makes more sense for this macro to always produce a target
that triggers a transition. This commit specifies and implements

subject: [ci] Initialize bazelCacheGcpKeyPath in execute_verilated_tests
body:
I noticed a surprising error message in a CI run for a PR:
`bazelCacheGcpKeyPath: command not found`. For CI runs on the master
branch, that error message is nowhere to be found.

milesdai@opentitan.org pointed out that the step that sets the variable,
named "GCP key path", only runs when the current branch is "master".

It seems that Azure Pipelines has not been replacing the macro
expression `$(bazelCacheGcpKeyPath)` with a value for PR runs because
the variable was undefined. Then, at runtime, bash attempted to
interpret the expression as command substitution, but complained because
the command does not exist. (Why didn't this prevent "Build & execute
tests" from running the verilator tests? Because `export` masked the
error! See SC2155[^0].)

This hypothesis is backed up by the Azure Pipelines docs[^1]:

> If there's no variable by that name, then the macro expression does
> not change. For example, if $(var) can't be replaced, $(var) won't be
> replaced by anything.

More context on the error from the PR run:

```
Starting: Build & execute tests
==============================================================================
Task         : Bash
Description  : Run a Bash script on macOS, Linux, or Windows
Version      : 3.226.2
Author       : Microsoft Corporation
Help         : https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/tasks/utility/bash
==============================================================================
Generating script.
========================== Starting Command Output ===========================
/usr/bin/bash /azp/agent/_work/_temp/d9fb36b5-1d40-4f45-8f7c-9f762b39e3e4.sh
++ bazelCacheGcpKeyPath
/azp/agent/_work/_temp/d9fb36b5-1d40-4f45-8f7c-9f762b39e3e4.sh: line 2: bazelCacheGcpKeyPath: command not found
+ export GCP_BAZEL_CACHE_KEY=
+ GCP_BAZEL_CACHE_KEY=
+ ci/scripts/run-verilator-tests.sh
```

[^0]: https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/SC2155
[^1]: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/variables?view=azure-devops&tabs=yaml%2Cbatch#macro-syntax-variables

Signed-off-by: Dan McArdle <dmcardle@opentitan.org>

subject: [tock] Describe tock/libtock dependencies
body:
Provide dependencies on tock and libtock in a way that supports
software releases and local development.  Previously, we tried to use
`crate_universe` to provide the tock/libtock deps, but `crate_universe`
does not allow depending on an arbitrary github archive or a local
filepath.  We need to depend on arbitrary github archives because the tock
and libtock crates are not available in a crate index (like crates.io).
`crate_universe` does support depending on arbitrary git commits, however,
the OpenTitan repo supports building in airgapped mode and bazel does
not support arbitrary git commits for airgapped builds.

In order to support arbitrary archives and local development paths, we
create a repository rules that permits download+extract or symlinking to
a local directory tree.  The rule also supports adding additional files
into the target bazel repository to build a hierarchy of BUILD targets.
We also provide a reasonable `crate_build` macro to construct BUILD
files with a reasonable `rust_library` rule.

1. Add a `symlink_tree` utility to create a symlinked clone of a local
   path.
2. Add a `bare_repository` rule that can either download and archive or
   link to a local subdirectory and insert a user-specified BUILD
   hierarchy into the repository.
3. Add a repository for `lowRISC/tock` and construct an appropriate
   BUILD hierarchy.
4. Add a repository for `tock/libtock-rs` and construct an appopriate
   BUILD hierarchy.

Signed-off-by: Chris Frantz <cfrantz@google.com>

subject: [opentitantool] Allow configuration of SPI chip select
body:
With this change, and accompanying modification to HyperDebug firmware,
OpenTitanTool is able to use named chip select pins in conjunction with
the hard-wired SPI data and clock pins.

This can either be achieved by command line arguments, such as:
`opentitantool spi --bus=S2 --chip-select=IOA7 sfdp`

or though declaring named spi target devices:
```
"spi": [
  {
    "name": "BOOTSTRAP",
    "bits_per_sec": 8000000,
    "chip_select": "CN10_6",
    "alias_of": "QSPI"
  },
  {
    "name": "TPM",
    "bits_per_sec": 250000,
    "chip_select": "IOA7",
    "alias_of": "QSPI"
  }
],
```

In either case, the operator must ensure that prior to issuing SPI
transactions, the chosen chip select pin is in `PushPull` mode and high
level, (and that the data and clock pins are in `Alternate` mode, but
that is the HyperDebug power-on default).

https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromiumos/platform/ec/+/4739792
