Prior to this commit, a case statement in the Controller transceiver
listed `State_ClkLoAwaitD`, `State_ClkHiSampleD` and `State_ClkHiAwaitD`
twice.  The second listing had no effect but made the case items
overlap.

This commit removes the duplicates.  The behavior does not change.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Break loop through command completion
body:
Prior to this commit, `cmd_complete` in the Controller FSM depended on
`proceed`, which in `DATCapt` depends on a Response Queue write.  That
write shares the buffer arbiter with the Command Queue read that
`cmd_complete` drives.  AscentLint flags the resulting combinational
loop as an error.

This commit uses `trx_dready_i` instead of `proceed`, which equals it in
all states where `cmd_complete` uses it.  This breaks the loop without
changing the behavior.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Handle all FSM states explicitly
body:
Prior to this commit, only `default` branches handled `ErrFatal` in the
Controller FSM, `State_Stop` in the Controller transceiver, and
`State_Idle` and `State_TxNACKDDR` in the Target transceiver.

This commit adds explicit branches with the same next states.  The
behavior does not change.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Drop reset task in Standby Controller
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_stby_cr_regs` reset its outputs through a
task, which AscentLint flags as an error.

This commit assigns localparams with the reset values instead.  The
reset values are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Use max address of Target IBI buffer
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_core` took both bounds of the Target IBI
buffer from `TARG_IBI_CONFIG.MIN_ADDR`, so the buffer held a single word
regardless of `TARG_IBI_CONFIG.MAX_ADDR`.

This commit takes the maximum address from `TARG_IBI_CONFIG.MAX_ADDR`.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Rename FIFO bounds to `min/max_addr`
body:
Prior to this commit, the FIFO address bounds were named `min` and
`max`, which are Verilog-AMS keywords that AscentLint flags as errors.

This commit renames them to `min_addr` and `max_addr`, as in the
register fields.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Rename parameter `Event` of `i3c_intr`
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_intr` had a parameter `Event`, which is a
Verilog-1995 keyword that AscentLint flags as an error.

This commit renames it to `EventType`.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Rename Controller trx `tm_cycles`
body:
Prior to this commit, a signal in the Controller transceiver had the
name of the function `tm_cycles`, which AscentLint flags as an error.

This commit renames the signal to `phase_cycles`.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [prim] Add `ceil_udiv` to `prim_util_pkg`
body:
Prior to this commit, `prim_util_pkg` provided only `ceil_div`, which
takes signed `integer` operands.  Callers with unsigned operands, such
as frequencies and durations, needed signedness casts.

This commit adds `ceil_udiv`, which takes and returns 32-bit unsigned
values.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Use `ceil_udiv` from `prim_util_pkg`
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_timing_pkg` duplicated a ceiling division
and used it before declaring it, which AscentLint flags as an error.

This commit uses `prim_util_pkg::ceil_udiv` instead.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Name the types of local structs
body:
Prior to this commit, three local variables had anonymous struct types,
which AscentLint flags as errors.

This commit declares a named packed struct type for each of them.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Select DAT read word via word array
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_dat` selected the read word through
part-selects of a struct, which AscentLint flags as an error.

This commit indexes an array of two 32-bit words instead.  The read data
does not change.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Remove unused `dat_wdata_packed`
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_dat` declared `dat_wdata_packed` but never
used it, which AscentLint flags as an error.

This commit removes it.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Connect queue arrays via patterns
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_core` connected unpacked-array ports of
`i3c_queues` with concatenations, which AscentLint treats as packed
vectors and flags as errors.

This commit uses assignment patterns with the same element order.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Remove unused parameters
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_cmd_decode` and `i3c_controller_ccc` declared
parameters that they did not use, which AscentLint flags as errors.

This commit removes `NumDATEntries` and `DATAddrW` from `i3c_cmd_decode`
and `DataWidth` from `i3c_controller_ccc`.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Stop HDR Restart detection self-clear
body:
Prior to this commit, `i3c_core` tied `hdr_restart_done` to
`hdr_restart_det`, so the pattern detector cleared each detection
asynchronously right after setting it.  AscentLint flags this loop as an
error.  Nothing consumes the detection yet (see #31035).

This commit ties `hdr_restart_done` to 0, so the detection stays set
until the detector is disabled, and states in the TODO how the Target
logic shall acknowledge detections.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/lint] Waive errors on bus-derived clocks
body:
Prior to this commit, AscentLint flagged as errors the intended use of
SCL and SDA as clocks, including their gating, scan muxing and
synchronization, and their use as data and resets.

This commit waives these errors with a justification for each.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

This commit waives these errors with a justification for each.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/lint] Waive unused Controller role parameters
body:
Prior to this commit, AscentLint flagged as errors that `i3c_controller`
and `i3c_controller_trx` do not use `PrimaryCtrl` and `SecondaryCtrl`.
The Controller does not distinguish these roles yet (see #31308).

This commit waives these errors.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Use `unique case` throughout
body:
Prior to this commit, no case statement of the I3C IP had a `unique` or
`priority` qualifier, which AscentLint flags as errors.

This commit adds `unique` to all of them.  Their items are mutually
exclusive and all have a `default`, so the behavior does not change.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Use `logic` instead of `bit` and `int`
body:
Prior to this commit, several declarations used the two-state types
`bit` and `int`, which AscentLint flags as errors.

This commit replaces them with `logic` types and gives `rdata_src_e` an
explicit base type.  In `i3c_timing_pkg`, it adds the casts that this
requires, calculates `tclh` without arithmetic inside a shift, and
removes the unused variable `unity`.  The timing values are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Make width conversions explicit
body:
Prior to this commit, many expressions relied on implicit width
extension or truncation, which AscentLint flags as errors.

This commit makes these conversions explicit.  Comparisons whose operand
widths depend on parameters now use 32 bits.  The behavior does not
change.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/rtl] Avoid mixing signed and enum values
body:
Prior to this commit, some expressions mixed signed and unsigned values,
indexed enum values, passed enum values as integer parameters, or
negated by explicit two's complement.  AscentLint flags these as errors.

This commit uses unsigned casts and literals, `broadcast_ccc` and size
casts for enum values, `int` casts for parameters, and unary minus.  The
behavior does not change.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

This commit wraps it.

This commit waives these errors with a justification for each.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/lint] Waive intended lint warnings
body:

constructs, e.g., flops driven by constants and indices wider than the

This commit waives these warnings with a justification for each.

subject: [i3c/rtl] Pass default FIFO bounds positionally
body:

pattern with labels.  AscentLint ignores the labels and reports the
pattern as incomplete, which fails its run.  The default value of
`DefMin` also had only one element.

This commit passes the values positionally in FIFO order, naming each
FIFO in a comment, and sets all elements of the default value to zero.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [fpga,earlgrey] Fix marginal timing after routing
body:
Prior to this commit, the build-time optimized CW340 flow placed the
design without timing and skipped `phys_opt_design`.  A marginal path
could then miss timing by a few tens of picoseconds after routing, and
the post-route hook failed the build.  This happened for paths
unrelated to the change under test, depending on placement: a setup
violation in `clk_main` (see #31704) and a removal violation on an
`i2c1` reset (see #31767).

This commit adds two steps to the post-route hook, each run only if
the slack is still negative.  First, `phys_opt_design -directive
AggressiveExplore` fixes setup violations.  Second, `route_design
-directive Explore` also fixes hold violations.  On the routed
checkpoints of the two failing builds, the first step turned the setup
slack from -0.039 ns into +0.301 ns, and the second step turned the
hold slack from -0.039 ns into +0.030 ns in about 7 minutes.  The
routed checkpoint, the routed timing report and the bitstream are
written after this hook from the design in memory, so they include the
fixes.  A build that meets timing does not take longer.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [cheriot,rtl] Pipeline TBRE read responses
body:
Prior to this commit, the mover of the revocation engine (TBRE) passed
read responses through its payload FIFO.  This made a single-cycle path
from the read data of the main SRAM, through the revocation lookup of
the TRVK filter and the tag clear of the mover, through the tag filter
and the tag mux, to the meta SRAM and its local escalation.  On the
CW340 FPGA, this path took about 41 ns (not always; dependent on
placement) of the 41.667 ns period of `clk_main` and failed timing.

This commit disables pass-through on `u_prim_fifo_sync_payload`, so the
FIFO registers every read response.  The FIFO keeps its depth of
`MaxInflight`.  It still never refuses a response, as it holds at most
the words in flight minus the outstanding reads.  The order of the
responses and the tag and error of each response do not change.  The
window in which a core write marks a capability stale grows by one
cycle and still meets the window of the tag clear squash in
`cheriot_mem_sys`.

A word now resolves one cycle later, so with `TbreInflight = 2` the
engine reads at most two words every three cycles from the main SRAM.
Raising `TbreInflight` could restore the full rate later, but is not
done here to minimize time to solution.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [clkmgr,dv] Run clk_i at its source frequency
body:
Prior to this commit, the clkmgr testbench randomized the frequency of
the primary clock `clk_i` with `DV_COMMON_CLK_CONSTRAINT`, i.e. between
about 5 and 100 MHz.  In Darjeeling, `clk_i` is the io clock, which runs
at 250 MHz, and the aon clock runs at 62.5 MHz.  The testbench uses that
aon frequency, so `clk_i` was often slower than the aon clock, which
never happens in the chip (see #27075).  With such a `clk_i`,
`clkmgr_frequency_timeout`, `clkmgr_stress_all` and
`clkmgr_stress_all_with_rand_reset` failed with:

  UVM_ERROR (clkmgr_base_vseq.sv:320) [clkmgr_frequency_timeout_vseq]
  Mismatch for timeout recoverable error, expected 0b10, got 0b00

These failures show once the measurements run on Darjeeling (see
#30867).

There were two causes.  First, `clkmgr_frequency_timeout_vseq` reads
`RECOV_ERR_CODE` a fixed 12 aon cycles after it stops a measured clock.
With a slow `clk_i`, this did not cover the crossing of the timeout into
the `clk_i` domain, and the read returned before the error bit was set.
Second, the timeout level in the aon domain can be shorter than one
`clk_i` period.  `clkmgr_meas_chk` samples it with a 2-flop
synchronizer, so with CDC randomization the timeout could be missed.

Earl Grey and English Breakfast were not affected: their `clk_i` is the
io_div4 clock and their testbench aon clock runs at 200 kHz, far below
any randomized `clk_i` frequency.

This commit adds the clkmgr ipgen parameter `primary_clk`, the name of
the source clock of clkmgr's `clk_i`, which topgen takes from the
clkmgr instance's `clock_srcs`.  The clkmgr env cfg template uses it to
constrain `clk_freq_mhz` to the frequency of that source clock, like
`otp_ctrl_env_cfg` overrides `clk_freq_mhz_c`.  This sets `clk_i` to
250 MHz in Darjeeling and to 24 MHz in Earl Grey and English Breakfast.
If `primary_clk` does not name a source or derived clock, the template
fails with an error that lists the valid names.

This commit also regenerates the clkmgr ipconfig and DV env cfg of all
three tops.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/data] Exclude volatile fields from CSR checks
body:
Prior to this commit, the following register fields, which hardware
updates without a software write to the field, had no CSR test
exclusions:

- `HC_CONTROL.BUS_ENABLE` reads back the controller state.  After
  software writes 0, it remains 1 until the controller has become
  inactive.
- `STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR.DYNAMIC_ADDR` and `DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID` take the
  value that software writes to `CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR` while the
  block is the Active Controller.
- `TARG_QUEUE_STATUS_LEVEL.ASYNC_EVT_LVL` is a live queue level, which
  e.g. a Bus Idle event increments while the Target is enabled.

`csr_rw`, `csr_aliasing` and `same_csr_outstanding` could thus fail,
depending on the seed.

This commit excludes these fields from the check that they cannot pass
in the non-init CSR tests.  `csr_hw_reset` still checks the reset
values of all of them.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/dv] Add block-level UVM testbench
body:
Prior to this commit, the I3C IP had no block-level testbench, so the
common CSR and memory test suites, on which the D1 checklist item
`IP_INSTANTIABLE` depends, could not run.

This commit adds a `cip_base`-derived UVM environment, a testbench top,
the SVA bind file with the generated CSR assertions, a testplan that
imports the common CSR testplan, and a sim cfg with the common CSR
tests.

The testbench instantiates the DUT with the Earl Grey parameters and
clocks the AON domain at 200 kHz.  The base vseq resets the AON domain
together with the main domain, so that the CSR tests cover the
registers of both domains.

The I3C bus model connects the SCL and SDA drivers, pull-ups and
high-keepers to the respective DUT outputs.  Board-level pull-ups keep
the bus at a defined level when the DUT disables all of these; the env
enables them only for tests that request this with
`+en_board_pullup=1`.  All common CSR tests do so, because they write
random values to `PHY_CONFIG`.

The env adjusts the RAL to the DUT configuration: it sets the reset
values of the Virtual Targets that the DUT does not implement, as
`chip_env_cfg` does, and the reset value of `TARG_STATUS.NUM_TARGETS`.

The scoreboard does not model the I3C functionality yet.  It checks
reads from the memory windows, except from the HCI and TTI queue
ports, and compares only the stored bits of DAT and DCT entries.  As
the queues store their data in the message buffer, an interface
observes the writes to the message buffer memory, and the scoreboard
does not check message buffer words that the hardware has written
since the last software write.  The scoreboard also predicts
`INTR_STATE` from the writes to `INTR_TEST` and checks it while the
hardware cannot signal an interrupt.

`csr_mem_rw_with_rand_reset` accesses the queue ports while it runs
`csr_rw`.  These accesses let the hardware change fields of
`BUFFER_STATUS` and `TARG_PIO_CONTROL`, so the env excludes these
fields from the read checks in this test only.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c/dv] Add memory tests
body:
Prior to this commit, the block-level testbench did not run the common
memory tests.

This commit adds `mem_walk` and `mem_partial_access` to the sim cfg and
the common memory testplan to the testplan.

The generic memory walk (`uvm_mem_walk_seq`) covers only the message
buffer window:

- `HCI_PORTS` and `TTI_PORTS` are queue ports, not storage: a read
  returns a queue entry rather than the data written to the same
  address.
- The DAT and the DCT do not store the reserved fields of their
  entries, which read as zero.

`i3c_csr_mem_walk_seq` replaces `csr_mem_walk_seq` and additionally
walks the DAT and the DCT, comparing only the stored bits of each word.
`mem_partial_access` accesses all windows, and the scoreboard checks
the read data as it does for `csr_mem_rw_with_rand_reset`.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [i3c] Check reset values of volatile CSRs
body:
Prior to this commit, 27 registers or fields that hardware updates
were excluded from all CSR checks, including the reset value check of
`csr_hw_reset`.  Their reset values are deterministic, though, and
three of them were wrong in `i3c.hjson`: `TARG_BUF_STATUS_LEVEL` and
`TARG_TX_QUEUE_STATUS_LEVEL` reported a reset value of 0 for free
levels, which are non-zero after reset.

This commit restricts the exclusions of 25 of these registers and
fields to the non-init CSR tests, so that `csr_hw_reset` checks their
reset values, and corrects the reset values of `IBI_FREE_LVL`,
`TX_DESC_FREE_LVL` and `TX_BUF_FREE_LVL`.  It regenerates
`i3c_reg_pkg.sv` and `registers.md` accordingly.

The Virtual Targets that an instance does not implement report free
levels of zero.  `chip_env_cfg` and `i3c_env_cfg` thus set the reset
value of `TARG_TX_QUEUE_STATUS_LEVEL` to zero for them, as they do for
the Tx buffer and Tx descriptor queue state.

`PRESENT_STATE_DEBUG` and `TARG_STATE_DEBUG` reflect the SCL and SDA
pin levels, which the chip-level simulation does not drive, so they
remain excluded from all checks in `i3c.hjson`.  The block-level
testbench drives the pins, so `i3c_env_cfg` restricts their exclusions
to the non-init CSR tests.

`u_<inst>_part_primary` and `u_<inst>_part_secondary`, so the RAL path
of a split IP pointed to a nonexistent instance.  This affected AST,
whose path was `u_ast` while topgen instantiates `u_ast_part_primary`.

This commit sets the HDL path root of a split IP to its primary
partition instance, which holds the register block.

subject: [pwrmgr,dv] Derive wake-up lists from `NumWkups`
body:
Prior to this commit, the `pwrmgr` DV environment hard-coded the six
Earl Grey wake-up sources: `pwrmgr_if` assigned `wakeup_en` and
`wakeup_status` from entries 5 to 0, and `wakeup_e` listed six names
in a fixed order.  This did not match tops with a different wake-up
list, such as Darjeeling and English Breakfast with three wake-ups,
and it would break with any change to the Earl Grey wake-up list.

This commit assigns `wakeup_en` and `wakeup_status` in a loop over
`NumWkups` and generates `wakeup_e` from the wake-up list of the
top-level.  It regenerates the `pwrmgr` DV collateral of all tops.

subject: [i3c] Make I3C a split IP with the reset detector
body:
Prior to this commit, the I3C IP exposed the interface to its Target
Reset Detector (`rstdet_enable`, `rstdet`) as inter-module signals, but
no top-level instantiated `i3c_reset_detector` (see #31679).  The
detector must be able to sit in a different power domain than the rest
of the IP, so that it can wake the chip from deep sleep.

This commit declares I3C as a split IP:

- The primary partition, `i3c_part_primary`, is the former `i3c`
  module.  It keeps the register interface and all Controller and
  Target logic.
- The secondary partition, `i3c_part_secondary`, wraps
  `i3c_reset_detector`.  It has its own SCL and SDA inputs
  (`rstdet_scl`, `rstdet_sda`), a wake-up request (`rstdet_wkup_req`)
  and a reset request for the I3C peripheral (`rstdet_target_rst`).
  It does not expose `chip_reset_o`, so that an external Controller
  cannot reset the chip.  Its scan inputs are tied off, as scan/DFT
  signals exist only in the primary partition (TODO(#31335)).
- `rstdet_enable` and `rstdet` become intra-IP connections between
  the partitions.
- The AON clock and reset are listed in both partitions: reggen
  resolves the `async` clock of the `RESET_DET_*` registers only in
  the primary partition.

`i3c` is renamed to `i3c_part_primary` rather than wrapped, because
the chip RAL expects the register block `u_reg` directly below the
primary partition instance.  A wrapper would add a hierarchy level and
require a different `hier_path` at chip and block level.  No block DV
testbench, FPV bind or chip-level path references the `i3c` module, so
the rename only affects the core file list, its `toplevel` and two
AscentLint waiver locations.

The regenerated `i3c_reg_pkg.sv` gains `NumAlertsPrimary` and
`NumAlertsSecondary`; `i3c_reg_top.sv` is unchanged.

The documentation now describes the reset detector as the secondary
partition instead of a module outside the IP.  The integration notes
describe the two partitions and how to connect the secondary one,
including the detector's own SCL and SDA inputs.  The programmer's
guide notes that software must route the detector inputs to the same
pads as the I3C bus, and the implementation status lists the open
points of the detector.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [top_earlgrey] Instantiate I3C reset detectors
body:
Prior to this commit, `top_earlgrey` instantiated `i3c0` and `i3c1`
without their Target Reset Detectors, leaving `rstdet_enable_o` and
`rstdet_o` unconnected and tying `rstdet_i` to its default (see

This commit configures both I3C instances as split IPs:

- `i3c0` has its primary partition in the Main power domain and its
  reset detector in the Aon domain, so that it can wake the chip from
  deep sleep.
- `i3c1` has both partitions in the Main domain.

Both detectors run on the AON peripheral clock and the `lc_aon` reset
of their power domain.

The I3C wake-ups take `pwrmgr` wake-up indices 0 and 1, so the indices
of all other wake-up sources shift by 2.  The detector inputs take
`pinmux` peripheral inputs 50 to 53, so the inputs from
`SpiDeviceTpmCsb` on shift by 4.  This commit adapts the users of
these indices:

- The chip-level all-wake-ups sequence waits for wake-up sources 2 to
  4 and checks these indices against `pwrmgr_reg_pkg`.
- The `pwrmgr` all-wake-ups tests get an I3C entry that is always
  skipped, because the test environments cannot send a Target Reset
  Pattern yet.
- The `dif_pwrmgr` unit test expects eight wake-up sources.

It also points the clock and reset connectivity checks to the
`u_i3c<n>_part_primary` instances and adds checks for the
`u_i3c<n>_part_secondary` instances.  In the CW340 FPGA constraints,
it pins the `pinmux` input selects of the detectors to the same pads
as those of their I3C instance, as for the existing I3C inputs, so that
no other pad clock propagates into the detectors.

Finally, it waives the AscentLint findings from the detector.  The
detector has no free-running clock: SCL and SDA from the pads clock
it, and asynchronous resets clear it.

The I3C section of the Earl Grey chip specification now describes the
detectors instead of stating that they are not instantiated.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

subject: [top_earlgrey,top_englishbreakfast,fpga] Use flip-flop Ibex register files
body:
RegFileFPGA maps Ibex's register file to LUT RAM, which is not reset.
With SecureIbex, a reset between the main core's register write and the
lockstep shadow core's leaves data and ECC out of step until that
register is written again; resets do not clear it. The next read raises
a lockstep major alert and stops the core. On CW340 this locked up
certain tests when OpenOCD halted the hart ("Hart 0 failed to halt
during examine()").

English Breakfast has no SecureIbex, but switches too, so that enabling
SecureIbex there is safe.

subject: [hw,csrng] Reject Generate commands with glen = 0
body:
A Generate command must request at least one block, but nothing
enforced this. A Generate with glen = 0 returned a single block
without marking it as the last one, so the final update of Key and V
and the reseed counter increment were skipped, and the additional data
of the command was kept for the next Generate.

Reject such commands in the command stage once the instance is known
to be instantiated. They are acknowledged with the previously unused
CMD_STS_INVALID_GEN_CMD status, raise the new
CMD_STAGE_INVALID_GEN_CMD_ALERT, and their additional data is flushed
like that of any other invalid command.

subject: Merged PR 118100: UVM protocol error testcases
body:
Add testcases that randomly inject invalid/illegal mailbox register accesses during a regular mailbox flow.
Testcases are added to inject invalid register accesses for both SOC->UC and UC->SOC mailbox flows in this PR. (only APB invalid reg accesses are performed, to validate the protocol error path).
Invalid register accesses are defined (as in the integration spec) as writes to an register (or reads from dataout) at an unexpected stage of the flow (i.e., write to clear execute when the responder has not yet returned control to the sender).
The soc_ifc UVM bench also includes new code to initialize interrupts and service error events when they occur to restore the mailbox state.
Also added a fix for a minor issue in the mailbox - certain fsm 'arc' signals toggled in the incorrect state (not a functional issue, but a power optimization).

subject: [entropy_src] Keep applying fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow (#506)
body:
Keep applying fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow instead of pulsing. This commit is
a manual port of the following Opentitan commit:

b454878f2528b49318ff2b604cb8d59a6e59b0ea

Which is associated with
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/21640.

Original commit description:

This commit applies the fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow signal in case of an
overflow. It used to only send a pulse through the register but now
the signal is applied until the FIFO has been emptied once and is
receiving contiguous data again.
This commit also aligns the documentation for the FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW
register. The register is now not clearable by software. It instead
is cleared by hardware.

Signed-off-by: Miguel Osorio <miguelosorio@google.com>

subject: [DOC] Revise and detail TRNG configuration for integration spec (#861)
body:
This commit revises and expands the TRNG configuration documentation,
incorporating detailed explanations for both the initial ROM-based setup
and later FIPS-compliant configurations.

Key updates include:
- Clarified the internal TRNG's role in ROM for Control Flow Integrity
  (CFI) countermeasures, noting its non-FIPS-compliant nature at this stage.
- Provided detailed calculations and recommended example thresholds for
  the adaptive proportion test and repetition count test during ROM
  operation.
- Introduced a "FIPS considerations" section, which details:
    - The required TRNG re-initialization steps for FIPS compliance.
    - Comprehensive explanation of adaptive self-test window sizes
      (ENTROPY_TEST_WINDOW vs. ACTUAL_TEST_WINDOW).
    - Configuration options for `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` (aggregating per
      symbol vs. handling each noise source separately).
    - Formulas for configuring FIPS-compliant adaptive self-test thresholds.
- Added a "Recommended configuration" subsection under FIPS considerations
  for both adaptive and repetition count tests.

body:
* [rtl] Add CALIPTRA_PRIM_MODULE_NAME macro.

The `CALIPTRA_PRIM_MODULE_NAME(name)` macro is used to provide a mechanism
to replace the prim generic implementations for technology specific ones.

At compile time, the user has to provide the following definitions:

- CALIPTRA_PRIM_ROOT: Pointing to the directory implementing the technology
  specific prims.
- CALIPTRA_PRIM_MODULE_PREFIX: Definining the prim module name prefix.

For example, for name=buf and CALIPTRA_PRIM_MODULE_PREFIX=caliptra_prim_generic,
the result module name is `caliptra_prim_generic_buf`.

Note: Support for the `CALIPTRA_PRIM_ROOT` envar will be added in a follow up

subject: [TESTS] SHA3 external mu test (#956)
body:
* [TESTS] External mu test uses SHA3 block

This creates a check_external_mu function inside the
smoke_test_mldsa_external_mu test. Before invoking the external mu flow
in Adam's bridge it now calculates the external mu with the SHA3 engine
and compares this to the pre-computed value. If these match then it goes
through the normal MLDSA external mu flow as before.

* [TESTS] MLDSA smoke test fix vectors

Before these test vectors were reversed before going through the MLDSA
flow which adds about 10 minutes of simulation time on Verilator. This
commit reverses the constant vectors to avoid wasting this time. The
commit adjusts both the MLDSA test as well as the external mu variant.

* [TESTS] Message endianness now configurable

Also change the calls to the SHA3 start function in cshake, sha3,
interrupt and external mu tests.

* [TESTS] SHA3 external mu test added

This runs ACVP NIST KAT vectors through the newly added SHA3 block. The
test runs 12 vectors through the SHA3 block with public key and
processed message and compares it to a pre-computed value made by
dilithium-py.

Here are the original vectors:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/ACVP-Server/refs/heads/master/gen-val/json-files/ML-DSA-sigGen-FIPS204/internalProjection.json

* [TESTS] Confusing comment removed

* [TB] External mu forcing services

This implements 4 separate forcing sequences. These are necessary for
full random external mu testing. Here are the codes:
- 0xD0: force the public key into the SHA3 message FIFO.
- 0xD1: force the message into the SHA3 message FIFO.

registers are locked by SWWE while crypto engines are busy. The test
exercises three scenarios:

- HMAC and ECC KV WR_CTRL registers (write_entry, dest_valid) reject
  FW writes while busy_o is asserted, then accept writes after idle
- KV RD_KEY/BLOCK/SEED_CTRL registers reject FW writes while busy
- pcr_hash_extend field in KV read controls is permanently locked
  (SWWE=0) for HMAC, ECC, and AES engines

  and SHA512 engines

body:
* fixes kv crypto flow tests so that they don't pick KV slot 23 and hang the DOE

* Add boot flow transition enforcement for DICE key integrity

   Add hardware-enforced monitoring and access control for key vault slots
   across ROM->FMC->RT boot phase transitions.

   Boot flow monitor (caliptra_top.sv):
   - Detect transitions via ICCM bank read address matching
   - MuBi4-encoded signals for glitch resistance
   - Error on fetch without lock, out-of-order transition, or invalid state

   KV monitor and enforcement (kv.sv):
   - Validate dest_valid on DICE slots at each transition
   - Per-slot saturating write counters detect truncated derivation chains
   - HW-driven lock_wr/lock_use (hwset) per boot phase
   - Atomic slot clearing of unreferenced keys at transitions
   - Alert flushes all entries via CPTRA_HW_ERROR_FATAL.kv_error

   - 4 registers backed by caliptra_prim_subreg_shadow

subject: [RTL] Enhance HMAC-512 area/perf (#1274)
body:
* [RTL] Redesign HMAC-512 around single-SHA + LAST

Replace the dual sha512_masked_core architecture (H1 + H2) with a
single time-multiplexed engine. Adds an inner_digest capture register
so the surviving SHA reruns the outer pass over the captured H1 digest.

- hmac_core: 6-state FSM IDLE -> IPAD -> MSG -> OPAD -> HMAC -> DONE
  with a 4-way input mux on sha_block (ipad / msg / opad / hmac_padded);
  is_last_block flag latches LAST at IDLE so MSG knows whether to stop
  or continue to outer; shrink LFSR array from 12 to 6 to match the
  192-bit entropy seed.
- hmac: plumb the LAST command from the wrapper into hmac_core; remove
  the core_is_last_block gating on core_tag_we so tag_valid carries
  its natural meaning again.
- hmac_drbg: advance on rising edge of HMAC_ready instead of
  HMAC_tag_valid_edge so DRBG no longer relies on intermediate-block
  digest_valid pulses.

* [RDL] Add CTRL.LAST; shrink LFSR_SEED 12->6

- hmac_reg.rdl: add LAST field at bit 5 of HMAC512_CTRL; shrink
  LFSR_SEED array from 12 to 6 dwords (192-bit entropy)
- regenerate hmac_reg.sv, hmac_reg_pkg.sv, hmac_reg_uvm.sv
- regenerate integration caliptra_reg.h, caliptra_reg_defines.svh,
  caliptra_reg_field_defines.svh for both passive and subsystem modes

* [RTL] Restore CTRL_ENTROPY state in hmac_core

Bring back the serial CTRL_ENTROPY state that captures a fresh
sha512_masked digest of the entropy_block before IPAD. Remove the
dead `assign lfsr_entropy = lfsr_seed` and restore the full 4-mode
hashing-algorithm comment on mode_reg.

Cost: +178 cy per INIT relative to the previous single-SHA build:
  * +89 cy: dedicated CTRL_ENTROPY SHA call. In the old parallel
    H1+H2 design this entropy hash ran on H2 in parallel with H1's
    IPAD; with one SHA core this hop is now serial.
  * +89 cy: the OPAD hash. In the old design it ran on H2 in parallel
    with H1's message-block hash; on the single SHA core it is now
    serial with MSG (already discussed in prior review).

* [RTL] Drop modifier triggers; refine CTRL.LAST

* hmac.sv: drop last_reg from three gates where it must not appear
  (block_reg_lock release, key_mode_error, key_zero_error). LAST
  cannot start an operation on its own, so only init_reg | next_reg
  qualify as operation-start indicators.
* hmac_reg.rdl: rewrite HMAC512_CTRL.LAST so the field clearly reads
  as a modifier on INIT or NEXT rather than a standalone trigger.

* [VAL] Extend hmac_ctrl_tb for LAST modifier

Update the testbench to match the new HMAC-512 single-SHA control
surface and add semantic coverage for the LAST modifier and the
CTRL_ENTROPY abort path.

CTRL writes that finalize an op now include CTRL_LAST_VALUE (sourced
from HMAC_REG_HMAC512_CTRL_LAST_MASK so we stay aligned with the
regen'd field defines). LFSR seed width drops from 384 to 192 bits to
match the new 6-word LFSR_SEED register, and random_gen() /
write_seed() follow.

New tasks (one call per mode):
- hmac_three_block_test: INIT, NEXT, NEXT|LAST sequence, using the
  RFC 4868 / NIST CAVS HMAC-SHA-384 COUNT=1 vector; the HMAC-SHA-512
  tag is derived from the same key and message.
- last_alone_ignored_test: confirms a bare LAST write cannot start
  the engine and leaves no state behind.
- continuous_cmd_last_test: bombards CTRL with every command variant
  while BUSY and checks the final digest still comes out clean.
- zeroize_mid_op_test: ZEROIZE mid-op drops the engine back to IDLE
  and the next op runs normally.
- init_next_conflict_test: when INIT|NEXT|LAST arrive together, INIT
  wins and NEXT is silently dropped.

* [RTL] Parametrize hmac_core widths for reuse

Promote hardcoded SHA-512 widths in hmac_core to module parameters
so the same core can later be reused for HMAC-256. Defaults match
today's values, so HMAC-512 behavior is unchanged.

BLOCK_SIZE, KEY_SIZE, TAG_SIZE and LFSR_SEED_SIZE are now declared
in hmac_param_pkg and threaded through hmac_core's port widths,
internal signals, IPAD/OPAD pad generation, and the LFSR loop count.
hmac.sv binds these parameters explicitly from its localparams.

SHA-512-specific items (sha512_masked_core, mode_reg, FINAL_PAD and
ENTROPY_PAD literals, inner_digest [511:0]) intentionally remain
hardcoded.

* [RTL] Refactor hmac_core sha_block FSM and params

Address review feedback on hmac_core:

- Drop module parameter block; consume widths from hmac_param_pkg
  (BLOCK_SIZE, KEY_SIZE, TAG_SIZE, LFSR_SEED_SIZE). Add 384
  variant consts (HMAC384_KEY_SIZE/TAG_SIZE/KEY_PAD/TAG_PAD).
- Rename hmac_ctrl_last to hmac_ctrl_ff; it is a flopped copy of
  the command bits, not a "last" command.
- Split sha_block out of state_logic into its own per-state mux
  with default '0.
- Replace hardcoded SHA-512 widths in hmac_core.sv with pkg
  constants (inner_digest slice).
- Move IPAD, OPAD, HMAC384/512_FINAL_PAD and ENTROPY_PAD into the
  pkg; drive the LFSR loop bound from LFSR_SEED_SIZE/32.

Bit-exact for every reachable hmac_ctrl_ff state.

* [RTL] Parametrize hmac_drbg LFSR seed width

Add LFSR_LENGTH parameter (default 192) on hmac_drbg and narrow
the lfsr_seed port from REG_SIZE (384) to LFSR_LENGTH bits to
match the new hmac_core LFSR seed size. Update the standalone
TB widths to follow.

Use 192'(random_gen()) instead of random_gen()[191:0] on the seed
assignments; the part-select on a function-call return is rejected
by VCS R-2020.12-SP2 (and is only marginally legal SV-2017).

* [RTL] Use new pkg widths in hmac.sv and flag LAST-alone

Apply the hmac_param_pkg constants from the previous commit and
add the LAST-without-INIT/NEXT error:

- get_mask now uses HMAC384_TAG_SIZE / HMAC384_TAG_PAD instead of
  literal 15:12 / 511:128.
- key_mode_error key check uses HMAC384_KEY_SIZE/DATA_WIDTH
  instead of literal 128'b0. No HMAC384_*_DWORDS helpers; each
  derived width is used exactly once.
- Flag LAST without INIT or NEXT: edge-detect last_alone_error
  and hw-set error2_sts (sha256 convention: keep generic
  errorN_sts RDL names, semantic meaning lives in the RTL
  signal). Uses *_reg (KV-gated) sources so it cannot false-fire
  during KV-pending stalls; INIT|LAST and NEXT|LAST still work.

last_alone_error is purely combinational and is not folded into
error_flag. This matches sha256: its invalid_sha_op is also a
one-cycle combinational signal that only feeds error1_sts.hwset
and never blocks the engine. The RW1C status bit on the SW side
provides the stickiness firmware needs; the RTL signal stays
non-sticky so a stray LAST does not gate future digest writes.

* [VAL] Parametrize hmac_ctrl_tb and verify LAST error

- Import hmac_param_pkg in the bench and use BLOCK_SIZE,
  KEY_SIZE, TAG_SIZE, HMAC384_KEY_PAD, HMAC384_TAG_PAD in task
  signatures and reg decls. Add hmac_param_pkg.sv to the
  hmac_ctrl_tb compile.yml so the symbols resolve at vlogan.
- Fix HMAC-384 expected-tag padding: was HMAC384_KEY_PAD, should
  be HMAC384_TAG_PAD. Same value today, just the right name.
- Rename last_alone_ignored_test to last_alone_error_test and
  check ERROR2_STS after a LAST without INIT/NEXT to verify the
  new interrupt path. Follow-up valid op confirms the engine
  recovers.

* [CI] Update pr_timestamp and pr_hash stamps

* [RDL] Document KV polling contract for INIT/NEXT

INIT and NEXT pulses are masked when KV is not ready, matching
sha512's convention. Note in the field descriptions that SW must
poll HMAC512_KV_RD_KEY_STATUS.READY and HMAC512_KV_RD_BLOCK_STATUS.READY
before writing the bit, and clarify that STATUS.READY only tracks
the HMAC pipeline, not KV readiness.

No RTL change. Generated reg files do not embed field descriptions,
so no regen is needed.

* [RTL] Pulse tag_valid on intermediate blocks for save/restore prep

After a non-LAST CTRL_MSG block completes, pulse digest_valid before dropping to IDLE. Restores main's per-block tag_valid behavior in the refactored single-SHA hmac_core and exposes intermediate inner-hash H via the existing TAG register for future save/restore.

No new ports or output flags. All hmac.sv consumers (KV write, notif_cmd_done, kv_data_present_reset, dest_data_avail) keep using core_tag_we as in main; the final block overwrites intermediate H in KV.

Revert hmac_drbg edge detector to HMAC_tag_valid_edge/_last (matches main now that tag_valid pulses per block).

Verified: hmac_ctrl_tb, hmac_drbg_tb.

* [UVM] Add HMAC LAST modifier and last-alone test

Align the HMAC UVMF env with the new CTRL.LAST modifier and the
LAST-alone error path added in the HMAC redesign.

Driver BFM: issue INIT|LAST for single-block ops and NEXT|LAST for
the final block of multi-block ops, shrink LFSR_SEED writes from
12 to 6 words, and fix the inner-SHA msg_size to include the
1024-bit K^ipad block. Add a last_alone_error_test task that
issues a LAST-alone CTRL write followed by a legal hmac512 op so
the scoreboard still sees one expected/actual digest pair.

Transaction/interface: add op == 3'b100 (last_alone_op) and expose
last_alone_error_edge on HMAC_in_if for coverage sampling.

Predictor: handle op == 3'b100 by predicting the follow-up hmac512
digest so scoreboard MATCH proves clean recovery after the illegal
write.

Coverage: sample last_reg and the last_alone_error chain, and
replace hmac_cmd_cp with single-pulse bins for init, next,
last_alone_ignored, init_last and next_last so any RTL regression
that drops the detector is caught.

New test: HMAC_last_alone_error_test/_sequence run the BFM task
above and are registered in HMAC sim testlist.yaml and the nightly
random regression yml.

* [RTL] Flag HMAC LAST-alone error and drive LAST in flows

Wire last_alone_error directly from CTRL.LAST/INIT/NEXT bits
(SHA256 invalid_sha_op style) instead of the KV-gated *_reg
copies, so the error fires on every illegal LAST-alone write
regardless of KV state. error2_sts stickiness is preserved via
the existing RDL hwset path.

Update HMAC firmware flows to drive the new CTRL.LAST modifier:
single-block ops issue INIT|LAST, multi-block ops finish with
NEXT|LAST. Touches libs/hmac and consumer smoke tests.

Extend smoke_test_hmac_errortrigger with a stage that writes
LAST alone and confirms hmac_error fires via the ISR path, so
integration regression catches any regression dropping the new
detector.

* [RTL] Use LFSR_SEED_SIZE from hmac_param_pkg in ecc DRBG iface

* [RTL] Drop redundant hmac_param_pkg.sv from hmac_ctrl_tb target

hmac_ctrl_tb already requires hmac_ctrl, whose rtl target lists
hmac_param_pkg.sv. Re-listing it in the tb target was redundant
and forced the ADO promote pipeline's FILE LIST CHECK to regenerate
all ~99 .vf file lists.

* [VAL] update kv_boot_flow LFSR_SEED loop bound for 6-word seed

The HMAC512 LFSR_SEED register was shrunk from 12 dwords to 6 dwords
in the single-SHA redesign. kv_boot_flow.c still referenced the old
LFSR_SEED_11 constant, breaking the smoke_test_kv_boot_flow_monitor
compile on the L0 regression. Update the loop upper bound to
LFSR_SEED_5 to match the new register layout.

* [RTL] ICCM write hash measurement: autonomous arming

Remove firmware's responsibility for arming the SHA accelerator that
measures ICCM contents. The accelerator now self-triggers on the first
ICCM write the snoop sees.

* Delete MODE.ICCM_MODE field from sha512_acc_csr (sha512_acc_external_csr.rdl).
  ROM no longer has to write the arming bit before the firmware copy.
* sha512_acc_top.sv now derives iccm_mode autonomously:
  - On the first ICCM write the snoop sees (iccm_hash_dv_i), the live OR
    of iccm_armed and the snoop pulse drives iccm_mode high in the same
    cycle, capturing the first dword without a one-cycle slip.
  - A sticky iccm_armed flop latches on the same trigger (or on
    iccm_lock_i for the zero-length case) so iccm_mode stays high across
    the rest of the firmware copy.
  - iccm_armed is gated by ~iccm_mode_done so writes after PCR4/PCR5
    extend completes do not re-arm, and by ~soc_has_lock so SOC cannot
    suppress the measurement by pre-grabbing the SHA acc lock.
* Add LOCK.LOCK.hwclr and drive it from a new iccm_lock_acquire pulse,
  so HW autonomously claims the SHA acc lock the same cycle iccm_mode
  engages. The existing hwset path still releases the lock after the
  PCR4/PCR5 extend completes.

Coverage:

subject: [dvsim] Add initial dvsim support files to tools/dvsim/ (#1331)
body:
* [dvsim] Add initial dvsim support files to tools/dvsim/

This change lays down the initial scaffolding required to drive Caliptra
simulations with the lowRISC/OpenTitan dvsim tool. It introduces a tools/dvsim/
directory containing project-wide hjson configs, tool-specific hjson configs for
VCS/Xcelium/Questa, common coverage/xprop/UNR directive files, TCL helpers for
waves and coverage merging, a build/run Makefile, and a starter set of reusable
testplans. No DUT-specific *_sim_cfg.hjson files are added yet — this commit is
only the shared substrate that per-block sim configs will import_cfgs from.

What's added

Common project-wide hjson configs (imported by all sim cfgs)

- common_project_cfg.hjson — Project-level defaults consumed by
every *_sim_cfg.hjson: scratch_base_path/scratch_path layout, empty
build_pass_patterns / build_fail_patterns placeholders, exports for SCRATCH_PATH
and proj_root, and empty results-server hooks. Project/repo/doc/results-server
URLs are stubbed as empty strings for a downstream project to fill in.
- common_sim_cfg.hjson — The shared simulation flow definition. Sets flow: sim,
points flow_makefile at sim.mk, chains import_cfgs (common_project_cfg →
common_modes → fusesoc → {tool}.hjson), defines default build_dir / run_dir
layout, default UVM run_pass_patterns / run_fail_patterns, UVM verbosity
expansion table, default build_opts (UVM defines, SIMULATION,
DUT_HIER={dut_instance}), the default sim_tops/dut_instance scheme, canned
regressions (smoke, all, all_once, nightly), and per-tool coverage cfg file
pointers (VCS + Xcelium) so that individual DUT configs pick these up for free.
- common_modes.hjson — Reusable "sim modes" that layer on top of build_modes:
gui, gui_debug, waves, waves_off, cov (also injects +en_cov=1), profile, xprop,
loopdetect, build_seed (wraps +define+BUILD_SEED={seed} for reproducible
randomized builds), and a uvm_trace run mode. All are is_sim_mode: 1 so they
compose additively with each tool's build modes.
- fusesoc.hjson — Glue between dvsim and FuseSoC as the SV file-list generator:
sv_flist_gen_cmd: fusesoc, canonical sv_flist_gen_opts
(run --target=sim --setup --work-root=…), fusesoc_cores_root_dirs rooted at
{proj_root}/hw, and the .scr file dvsim will consume.

Tool-specific hjson configs

- vcs.hjson (366 lines) — Full VCS provider: SIMV/vlogan/vhdlan invocations,
+defines, wave/GUI/coverage/xprop/profile/UNR/loopdetect build modes,
coverage-related knobs (-cm, -cm_hier, exclusions), and hook-ins to the shared
vcs_*_cfg_file variables from common_sim_cfg.hjson.
- xcelium.hjson (269 lines) — Xcelium equivalent: xrun-based build/run commands,
wave/GUI/coverage/xprop/profile build modes, cov merge/report scripts, and paths
to Xcelium .ccf/tcl files under tools/xcelium/.
- questa.hjson (115 lines) — Questa provider (vlog/vopt/vsim invocations plus
wave/GUI/coverage build modes).

Build/run Makefile

- sim.mk — The flow_makefile dispatched to by dvsim. Provides build / run phases
with pre_build / post_build / pre_run / post_run hooks and glues in
sw_build_cmd, coverage-related targets, and (per tool) the compile + elaborate +
simulate steps.

Coverage / xprop / UNR directive files (per tool)

Under tools/dvsim/tools/vcs/:
- cover.cfg, cover_reg_top.cfg — hierarchical cov selection templates
- common_cov_excl.cfg — shared coverage exclusions
- fsm_reset_cov.cfg — FSM reset-state cov control
- unr.cfg — unreachable-analysis config
- xprop.cfg — X-propagation config

Under tools/dvsim/tools/xcelium/:
- common.ccf, cover.ccf, cover_reg_top.ccf, cover_reg_top_toggle_excl — coverage
config
- common_cov_excl.tcl, cov_merge.tcl, cov_report.tcl — coverage flow TCL
- unr.cfg — unreachable-analysis config

Shared TCL helpers

Under tools/dvsim/tools/:
- common.tcl — Shared TCL utility procs sourced by both simulators.
- sim.tcl — Simulator-agnostic driver TCL.
- waves.tcl — Wave-dumping directives (FSDB/SHM/etc.) invoked in waves mode.
- questa/sim.tcl — Questa-specific overrides for the simulate step.

Common testplans (consumed by the OpenTitan testplanner)

Under tools/dvsim/testplans/ — parameterized ({name}, {intf}) so a DUT testplan
can just import them:
- csr_testplan.hjson — Standard CSR testpoints: csr_hw_reset, csr_rw,
csr_bit_bash, csr_aliasing, plus the usual memory / mem-walk entries, all tagged
at V1.
- fpv_csr_testplan.hjson — FPV-oriented CSR testpoints for use with the formal
flow.
- intr_test_testplan.hjson — Reusable interrupt-testing testpoints (intr_test,
intr_pins, etc.).

Common test-list templates

Under tools/dvsim/tests/:
- csr_tests.hjson — Named test entries ({name}_csr_hw_reset, {name}_csr_rw,
{name}_csr_bit_bash, {name}_csr_aliasing, …) matching the CSR testplan, so a
block config can pull in the whole CSR suite by import + a small parameter set.
- intr_test.hjson — Matching template for the interrupt tests.

Misc

- .gitignore — Small addition (1 line) to ignore dvsim scratch output.

* [ENV] Add nix devshell for dvsim dependencies

Introduce a hermetic Python environment for the dvsim regression flow,

environments, which has led to hard-to-reproduce failures when
locally-installed package versions drift from those actually used in
regression. Pinning via a lockfile plus Nix makes the toolchain
byte-for-byte reproducible across machines and removes any dependence
on the host distribution's Python or pip cache.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Add nix devshell for reg-gen tooling

Introduce a second uv2nix-backed Python environment, this time for the
RDL register-generation tooling (systemrdl-compiler and the peakrdl
exporters used to regenerate register RTL and UVM RAL models). It is
exposed as a separate devshell so contributors regenerating registers
do not need to pull in the heavier dvsim dependency tree. Enter it
with `nix develop .#caliptra-reg-gen`.

The dependency versions are pinned to those documented in the
top-level README and used by the current CI regeneration flows, so
that outputs produced from this shell match what CI produces and
tracked generated files stay stable across contributors.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Pin compile-to-core in caliptra-dvsim devshell

Add the compile-to-core generator as a Python dependency of the
caliptra-dvsim devshell, pinned via a Nix flake input tracking its
main branch, and relock so its console script is installed into the
shell's virtualenv and available on PATH.

This is a prerequisite for the following commit, which wires the
generator into dvsim's fusesoc invocation as a pre_build step. Pinning
via a flake input (rather than a released version on PyPI) is
deliberate for now: the tool is still evolving in lockstep with the
dvsim integration in this branch, so a mutable main-branch pin is the
lightest way to iterate on both sides without a release cycle. This
should be swapped for a proper version pin once the tool stabilises.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Integrate compile-to-core as fusesoc pre_build

Wire the compile-to-core generator into dvsim's fusesoc flow as a
pre_build_cmd. Before fusesoc runs, the generator converts Caliptra's
existing compile.yaml files into fusesoc .core files under a scratch
directory, which is then passed to fusesoc via an added --cores-root
alongside the project's src/ and tools/dv-classes/ trees. The
sv_flist_gen_opts block is restructured accordingly so fusesoc sees
all three roots at setup time.

This is needed because the majority of the build description lives in
the MSFT-format compile.yaml files, which fusesoc cannot consume
directly; generating .core shims on the fly lets the dvsim flow reuse
the existing source-of-truth without duplicating it. The scratch dir
is placed under the dvsim scratch path so it is scoped to a single
build and cleaned up with the rest of the build artefacts.

The generated .f/.scr filelist path template is also updated to
mirror the transformation fusesoc applies when naming its output
files (colons in the VLNV identifier become underscores), which is
otherwise undocumented behaviour and easy to trip over on rename.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Exclude .lock files from the license header check script

These files are typically autogenerated by various build systems (e.g.
Cargo.lock, composer.lock, uv.lock, flake.lock) and as such do not need
a license header.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] dvsim build-scoped cores dir; git in .#caliptra-dvsim devshell

Changes address the Copilot review.

- tools/dvsim/fusesoc.hjson: generate the compile-to-core .core shims
  into {build_dir}/cores rather than {scratch_path}/cores, and point
  the matching --cores-root at the same location. {scratch_path} is
  shared across build modes, so concurrent builds could collide;
  {build_dir} scopes the shims per build, matching both the in-file
  comment and the commit that introduced them.

- flake.nix: make git available where it is needed.
  * commonShellHook runs `git rev-parse` to locate the repo root; it
    now references the binary directly via `${pkgs.lib.getExe pkgs.git}`
    so the hook resolves in both devshells without relying on git
    leaking in from the host.
  * The caliptra-dvsim shell additionally carries git as a package,
    because dvsim shells out to the git binary at runtime (branch and
    repo-root discovery in cli/run.py, plus GitPython in reporting).
    caliptra-reg-gen has no such dependency, so it is left out there.

subject: [RTL] Clear KV write controls on zeroize (#1410)
body:
* [RTL] Clear KV write controls on zeroize

A failed crypto operation never produces a result, so the KV write FSM
never starts and never clears KV_WR_CTRL.write_en via ~kv_*_ready. The
request stays armed and the next operation silently takes the KV path
with stale controls, zeroing the data that was expected.

Add zeroize to the hwclr term of the KV write control and write status
registers in HMAC, ECC and AES, matching the behavior already provided
to ABR by CALIPTRA_KV_WRITE_STATUS_ASSIGN in kv_macros.svh. The AES CLP
has no SW ZEROIZE register, so it uses debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch,
the zeroize source its KV clients already consume. SHA512 is not
affected: it has no key vault interface, and its KV client instances
are reused to drive the PCR vault.

Add three top-level assertions checking that write_en is deasserted
after zeroize.

Fixes https://github.com/chipsalliance/caliptra-rtl/issues/1159

decoded_reg_strb asserts on reads as well as writes, so guarding on it
alone also excused reads and swwe-blocked writes, leaving a verification
hole. Match the generated register priority exactly:
decoded_reg_strb && decoded_req_is_wr && swwe.

subject: [VAL] Gate MLDSA TB force/release on enable edges (#1412)
body:
* [VAL] Gate MLDSA TB force/release on enable edges

The MLDSA stimulus injection blocks in caliptra_top_tb_services expand,
through their generate loops, to roughly 3000 always @(negedge clk)
blocks. Each one performed an unconditional hierarchical release on
every negedge, even on tests that never exercise MLDSA, which added up
to billions of no-op release operations per simulation.

Register the injection enables and release only on the deasserting
edge. A release on an object that was never forced is a no-op, so the
behavior is unchanged.

Measured on caliptra_top_tb with assertions enabled:
  smoke_test_ecc_keygen  924.0s -> 589.6s  (-36.2%)
  smoke_test_ecc_sign    835.0s -> 574.5s  (-31.2%)
  smoke_test_ecc_verify 1115.8s -> 736.3s  (-34.0%)

Simulation time is identical in every case and smoke_test_mldsa_kat,
which exercises these injection blocks, still passes.

subject: [RTL] [SHA3] SHA3 zeroization (#1421)
body:
* [doc, sha3] Document the new SHA3 zeroize feature

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [rtl, sha3] Make the tl-ul adapter zeroizable

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [rtl, sha3] Make SHA3 zeroizable

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [dv, sha3] Add SHA3 zeroization test

This commit adds a test that aims to test the new zeroization feature.
The test consists of three hashing operations and performs the following steps:
- Run a initial hash and check if the digest matches the test vector
- Zeroize and run another hash operation to check if SHA3 computes the correct
  result or if residual state remains and the digest turns out incorrect
- Make SHA3 absorb the same message
- Zeroize again (but this time not in the idle state)
- Compute the same hash again and see if SHA3 still computes the correct digest.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [rtl,entropy_combiner] Make SHA3 inside entropy_combiner zeroizable

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [rtl,entropy_combiner] Make entropy_combiner zeroizable

This commit adds zeroization functionality to entropy_combiner.
Zeroize clears all internal state except for configuration registers.

Outstanding handshakes with CSRNG don't cause a violation.
entropy_combiner simply clears and handles the request again as if it
just came in fresh. This is possible since CSRNG has to keep req applied
until acked.

Outstanding handshakes with entropy source can't be handled the same way
since req needs to stay high until entropy source acks. When this is the
case we can just stay in the combiner_st_req_entropy state and clear any
internal state. The operation will continue as if nothing happened.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [dv, entropy_combiner] Add zeroization test cases

Add four cases to entropy_combiner_es_csrng_tb that zeroize the combiner
through debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch in different states of a combine
and check that nothing hangs:

- idle, before the CSRNG instantiate
- CSRNG has requested entropy, both entropy_src requests outstanding
- ES0 seed captured, ES1 request outstanding
- both seeds captured, SHA3 running and the CSRNG ack outstanding

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

subject: [rtl,entropy_src] Add ENTROPY_SRC zeroization (#1433)
body:
* [rtl,entropy_src] Use ot_sha3 as SHA3 conditioner

entropy_src used its own copy of the SHA3 engine in src/kmac, while the
SHA3 accelerator and the entropy combiner use the ot_sha3 copy in
src/sha3. The two copies only differ by the module names and the zeroize
support added to ot_sha3.

Move the SHA3 core files into a new ot_sha3 component, required by both
sha3_ctrl and entropy_src, and switch entropy_src to ot_sha3 with
zeroize tied off.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [rtl,entropy_src] Add zeroization

Add a debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch input and an
ENTROPY_SRC_CTRL.ZEROIZE register to entropy_src, aligned with
SHA3_CTRL.ZEROIZE. Either of them zeroizes entropy_src:
- all FIFOs are cleared, including their storage (resetOnClear)
- the main and ack state machines return to Idle
- all core flops, the health test state, the watermark and the alert
  counters are cleared
- the SHA3 conditioner is zeroized

The configuration registers, the interrupt and alert signaling and the
enable of the noise source are kept. The noise source keeps running and
an enabled entropy_src restarts on its own from Idle, so no seed is
delivered from the state before the zeroize. In the zeroize cycle, no
seed is acked and the data outputs read zero.

Add assertions for the zeroize behavior. Connect the input in
caliptra_top and tie it off in the testbenches.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [docs] Document entropy_src zeroization

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [tb,entropy_src] Add zeroize test cases

Drive debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch from the testbench and add test
cases:
- bypass mode: zeroize via ENTROPY_SRC_CTRL and via the input after the
  boot seed. entropy_src restarts and delivers a new boot seed, which is
  checked against the RNG bits received after the zeroize.
- FIPS mode: zeroize in each state of the main state machine, via
  ENTROPY_SRC_CTRL and with a multi-cycle zeroize. A new seed must be
  delivered after each zeroize.
Check that no seed is all-zero or equal to the previous seed.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [test] Add entropy_src zeroize smoke test

Run entropy_src in FIPS mode with the seeds routed to firmware and
zeroize it with a seed in the esfinal FIFO, during the startup and
continuous health tests, and back-to-back. Check that the FIFO is
cleared, that no error is raised and that entropy_src restarts and
delivers new, non-zero seeds. Add the test to the L0 regression.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [test,entropy_src] Add entropy_src smoke test with reference model

Add smoke_test_entropy_src, which runs entropy_src (ES0) in boot-time and
FIPS mode, each with 4-bit symbols and in single-lane mode. The seeds are
routed to firmware and compared against a new reference model
(src/entropy_src/tb/entropy_src_model.py), which reuses the conditioner
model of the entropy combiner tests and generates the expected seeds and
the health test thresholds (es_vectors.h) as described in the integration
specification.

physical_rng_deterministic now reloads its LFSR seed while disabled, like
physical_rng, so every configuration starts from the first sample.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [dv,zeroize] Add randomized zeroize tests

This commit adds randomized zeroize tests for sha3,
entropy_combiner and entropy_src.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

* [dv,sha3,es,es_combiner] Add coverage for zeroization

This commit adds coverage for the zeroization tests of
sha3, entropy_src and entropy_combiner.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

[RTL] Move synchronizers outside of DCLS (#1454)
body:
* [RTL] Move synchronizers outside of DCLS

The upstream VeeR EL2 core uses synchronizers inside the DCLS domain
to synchronize asynchronous signals. This causes issues for integrators
that use technology-specific sync cells that have randomized latencies
in their simulation models. In this case, DCLS mismatches can be
triggered.

Fix this by moving those synchronizers outside of the DCLS domain.

Closes #1445.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [VAL] Add randomized-latency synchronizer model and DCLS mismatch check

Add a simulation-only metastability model to rvsyncss and
rvsyncss_fpga (beh_lib.sv), enabled with +RV_SYNC_RAND_DELAY: each
input transition is randomly captured one cycle late. Every instance
is seeded from its hierarchical path, so the main and shadow core
copies resolve independently, like real sync cells. Synthesis builds
are unaffected.

Fail any test on a real main/shadow core divergence reported by the
lockstep comparator, independent of ss_dcls_en and the Caliptra mode.

Add c_intr_handler_sync_rand and smoke_test_wdt_sync_rand to the SS
L0 regression to check that interrupts, the timer and NMI cannot cause
false DCLS mismatches.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>
